iast:
śrī-ādi-nāthāya namo'stu tasmai
yenopadiṣṭā haṭha-yoga-vidyā  /
vibhrājate pronnata-rāja-yogam
āroḍhum icchor adhirohiṇīva
devanagari:
श्री-आदि-नाथाय नमोऽस्तु तस्मै
येनोपदिष्टा हठ-योग-विद्या  ।
विभ्राजते प्रोन्नत-राज-योगम्
आरोढुम् इच्छोर् अधिरोहिणीव
english: Salutation to Âdinâtha (Śiva) who expounded the knowledge of Haṭha Yoga, which like a staircase leads the aspirant to the high pinnacled Râja Yoga.

iast:
praṇamya śrī-guruṃ nāthaṃ svātmārāmeṇa yoginā  /
kevalaṃ rāja-yogāya haṭha-vidyopadiśyate
devanagari:
प्रणम्य श्री-गुरुं नाथं स्वात्मारामेण योगिना  ।
केवलं राज-योगाय हठ-विद्योपदिश्यते
english: Yogin Swâtmârâma, after saluting first his Gurû Srinâtha explains Haṭha Yoga for the attainment of Raja Yoga.

iast:
bhrāntyā bahumata-dhvānte rāja-yogam ajānatām  /
haṭha-pradīpikāṃ dhatte svātmārāmaḥ kṛpākaraḥ
devanagari:
भ्रान्त्या बहुमत-ध्वान्ते राज-योगम् अजानताम्  ।
हठ-प्रदीपिकां धत्ते स्वात्मारामः कृपाकरः
english: Owing to the darkness arising from the multiplicity of opinions people are unable to know the Râja Yoga. Compassionate Swâtmârâma composes the Haṭha Yoga Pradipikâ like a torch to dispel it.

iast:
haṭha-vidyāṃ hi matsyendra-gorakṣādyā vijānate  /
svātmārāmo'thavā yogī jānīte tat-prasādataḥ
devanagari:
हठ-विद्यां हि मत्स्येन्द्र-गोरक्षाद्या विजानते  ।
स्वात्मारामोऽथवा योगी जानीते तत्-प्रसादतः
english: Matsyendra, Gorakṣa, etc., knew Haṭha Vidyâ, and by their favour Yogî Swâtmârâma also learnt it from them.

iast:
śrī-ādinātha-matsyendra-śāvarānanda-bhairavāḥ  /
cauraṅgī-mīna-gorakṣa-virūpākṣa-bileśayāḥ
devanagari:
श्री-आदिनाथ-मत्स्येन्द्र-शावरानन्द-भैरवाः  ।
चौरङ्गी-मीन-गोरक्ष-विरूपाक्ष-बिलेशयाः
english: Sri Âdinâtha (Śiva), Matsyendra, Nâtha, Sâbar, Anand, Bhairava, Chaurangi, Mîna nâtha, Gorakṣanâtha, Virupâkṣa, Bileśaya.

iast:
manthāno bhairavo yogī siddhir buddhaś ca kanthaḍiḥ  /
koraṃṭakaḥ surānandaḥ siddhapādaś ca carpaṭiḥ
devanagari:
मन्थानो भैरवो योगी सिद्धिर् बुद्धश् च कन्थडिः  ।
कोरंटकः सुरानन्दः सिद्धपादश् च चर्पटिः
english: Manthâna, Bhairava, Siddhi Buddha, Kanthadi, Karantaka, Surânanda, Siddhipâda, Charapati.

iast:
kānerī pūjyapādaś ca nitya-nātho nirañjanaḥ  /
kapālī bindunāthaś ca kākacaṇḍīśvarāhvayaḥ
devanagari:
कानेरी पूज्यपादश् च नित्य-नाथो निरञ्जनः  ।
कपाली बिन्दुनाथश् च काकचण्डीश्वराह्वयः
english: Kânerî, Pûjyapâda, Nityanâtha, Nirañjana, Kapâli, Vindunâtha, Kâka Chandîśwara.

iast:
allāmaḥ prabhudevaś ca ghoḍā colī ca ṭiṃṭiṇiḥ  /
bhānukī nāradevaś ca khaṇḍaḥ kāpālikas tathā
devanagari:
अल्लामः प्रभुदेवश् च घोडा चोली च टिंटिणिः  ।
भानुकी नारदेवश् च खण्डः कापालिकस् तथा
english: Allâma, Prabhudeva, Ghodâ, Cholî, Tintiṇi, Bhânukî Nârdeva, Khanda Kâpâlika, etc.

iast:
ity ādayo mahāsiddhā haṭha-yoga-prabhāvataḥ  /
khaṇḍayitvā kāla-daṇḍaṃ brahmāṇḍe vicaranti te
devanagari:
इत्य् आदयो महासिद्धा हठ-योग-प्रभावतः  ।
खण्डयित्वा काल-दण्डं ब्रह्माण्डे विचरन्ति ते
english: These Mahâsiddhas (great masters), breaking the sceptre of death, are roaming in the universe.

iast:
aśeṣa-tāpa-taptānāṃ samāśraya-maṭho haṭhaḥ  /
aśeṣa-yoga-yuktānām ādhāra-kamaṭho haṭhaḥ
devanagari:
अशेष-ताप-तप्तानां समाश्रय-मठो हठः  ।
अशेष-योग-युक्तानाम् आधार-कमठो हठः
english: Like a house protecting one from the heat of the sun, Haṭha Yoga protects its practiser from the burning heat of the three Tâpas; and, similarly, it is the supporting tortoise, as it were, for those who are constantly devoted to the practice of Yoga.

iast:
haṭha-vidyā paraṃ gopyā yoginā siddhim icchatā  /
bhaved vīryavatī guptā nirvīryā tu prakāśitā
devanagari:
हठ-विद्या परं गोप्या योगिना सिद्धिम् इच्छता  ।
भवेद् वीर्यवती गुप्ता निर्वीर्या तु प्रकाशिता
english: A Yogî desirous of success should keep the knowledge of Haṭha Yoga secret; for it becomes potent by concealing, and impotent by exposing.

iast:
surājye dhārmike deśe subhikṣe nirupadrave  /
dhanuḥ pramāṇa-paryantaṃ śilāgni-jala-varjite  /
ekānte maṭhikā-madhye sthātavyaṃ haṭha-yoginā
devanagari:
सुराज्ये धार्मिके देशे सुभिक्षे निरुपद्रवे  ।
धनुः प्रमाण-पर्यन्तं शिलाग्नि-जल-वर्जिते  ।
एकान्ते मठिका-मध्ये स्थातव्यं हठ-योगिना
english: The Yogî should practise Haṭha Yoga in a small room, situated in a solitary place, being 4 cubits square, and free from stones, fire, water, disturbances of all kinds, and in a country where justice is properly administered, where good people live, and food can be obtained easily and plentifully.

iast:
alpa-dvāram arandhra-garta-vivaraṃ nātyucca-nīcāyataṃ
samyag-gomaya-sāndra-liptam amalaṃ niḥśesa-jantūjjhitam  /
bāhye maṇḍapa-vedi-kūpa-ruciraṃ prākāra-saṃveṣṭitaṃ
proktaṃ yoga-maṭhasya lakṣaṇam idaṃ siddhair haṭhābhyāsibhiḥ
devanagari:
अल्प-द्वारम् अरन्ध्र-गर्त-विवरं नात्युच्च-नीचायतं
सम्यग्-गोमय-सान्द्र-लिप्तम् अमलं निःशेस-जन्तूज्झितम्  ।
बाह्ये मण्डप-वेदि-कूप-रुचिरं प्राकार-संवेष्टितं
प्रोक्तं योग-मठस्य लक्षणम् इदं सिद्धैर् हठाभ्यासिभिः
english: The room should have a small door, be free from holes, hollows, neither too high nor too low, well plastered with cow-dung and free from dirt, filth and insects. On its outside there should be bowers, raised platform (chabootrâ), a well, and a compound. These characteristics of a room for Haṭha Yogîs have been described by adepts in the practice of Haṭha.

iast:
evaṃ vidhe maṭhe sthitvā sarva-cintā-vivarjitaḥ  /
gurūpadiṣṭa-mārgeṇa yogam eva samabhyaset
devanagari:
एवं विधे मठे स्थित्वा सर्व-चिन्ता-विवर्जितः  ।
गुरूपदिष्ट-मार्गेण योगम् एव समभ्यसेत्
english: Having seated in such a room and free from all anxieties, he should practise Yoga, as instructed by his guru .

iast:
atyāhāraḥ prayāsaś ca prajalpo niyamāgrahaḥ  /
jana-saṅgaś ca laulyaṃ ca ṣaḍbhir yogo vinaśyati
devanagari:
अत्याहारः प्रयासश् च प्रजल्पो नियमाग्रहः  ।
जन-सङ्गश् च लौल्यं च षड्भिर् योगो विनश्यति
english: Yoga is destroyed by the following six causes:—Over-eating, exertion, talkativeness, adhering to rules, i.e. , cold bath in the morning, eating at night, or eating fruits only, company of men, and unsteadiness.

iast:
utsāhāt sāhasād dhairyāt tattva-jñānāś ca niścayāt  /
jana-saṅga-parityāgāt ṣaḍbhir yogaḥ prasiddhyati
devanagari:
उत्साहात् साहसाद् धैर्यात् तत्त्व-ज्ञानाश् च निश्चयात्  ।
जन-सङ्ग-परित्यागात् षड्भिर् योगः प्रसिद्ध्यति
english: The following six bring speedy success:—Courage, daring, perseverance, discriminative knowledge, faith, aloofness. from company.
sourceNotes: Source reads tattva-jñānāś; expected sandhi in context is tattva-jñānāc (tattva-jñānāt + ca). No silent correction has been made.

The critical edition 1.16 has a substantially different list, including contentment and realization of truth. Correcting the isolated sandhi of the older transcription does not establish the critical reading. These edition differences must not be conflated.

iast:
ahiṃsā satyam asteyaṃ brahmacaryaṃ kṣamā dhṛtiḥ  /
dayārjavaṃ mitāhāraḥ śaucaṃ caiva yamā daśa
devanagari:
अहिंसा सत्यम् अस्तेयं ब्रह्मचर्यं क्षमा धृतिः  ।
दयार्जवं मिताहारः शौचं चैव यमा दश
english: The ten rules of conduct are: ahiṃsâ (non-injuring), truth, non-stealing, continence, forgiveness, endurance, compassion, meekness, sparing diet and cleanliness.

iast:
tapaḥ santoṣa āstikyaṃ dānam īśvara-pūjanam  /
siddhānta-vākya-śravaṇaṃ hrīmatī ca tapo hutam  /
niyamā daśa samproktā yoga-śāstra-viśāradaiḥ
devanagari:
तपः सन्तोष आस्तिक्यं दानम् ईश्वर-पूजनम्  ।
सिद्धान्त-वाक्य-श्रवणं ह्रीमती च तपो हुतम्  ।
नियमा दश सम्प्रोक्ता योग-शास्त्र-विशारदैः
english: The ten niyamas mentioned by those proficient in the knowledge of yoga are: Tapa, patience, belief in God, charity, adoration of God, hearing discourses on the principles of religion, shame, intellect, Tapa and Yajña.
sourceNotes: The draft’s “recitation” interprets a reading japo, supported by the critical edition’s appended verse 1.16_2, against the repeated tapo in this transcription. This is an editorial interpretation, not a literal rendering of every transmitted syllable.

iast:
haṭhasya prathamāṅgatvād āsanaṃ pūrvam ucyate  /
kuryāt tad āsanaṃ sthairyam ārogyaṃ cāṅga-lāghavam
devanagari:
हठस्य प्रथमाङ्गत्वाद् आसनं पूर्वम् उच्यते  ।
कुर्यात् तद् आसनं स्थैर्यम् आरोग्यं चाङ्ग-लाघवम्
english: Being the first accessory of Haṭha Yoga, âsana is described first. It should be practised for gaining steady posture, health and lightness of body.

iast:
vaśiṣṭhādyaiś ca munibhir matsyendrādyaiś ca yogibhiḥ  /
aṅgīkṛtāny āsanāni kathyante kānicin mayā
devanagari:
वशिष्ठाद्यैश् च मुनिभिर् मत्स्येन्द्राद्यैश् च योगिभिः  ।
अङ्गीकृतान्य् आसनानि कथ्यन्ते कानिचिन् मया
english: I am going to describe certain âsanas which have been adopted by Munîs like Vasiṣṭha, etc., and Yogîs like Matsyendra, etc.

iast:
jānūrvor antare samyak kṛtvā pāda-tale ubhe  /
ṛju-kāyaḥ samāsīnaḥ svastikaṃ tat pracakṣate
devanagari:
जानूर्वोर् अन्तरे सम्यक् कृत्वा पाद-तले उभे  ।
ऋजु-कायः समासीनः स्वस्तिकं तत् प्रचक्षते
english: Having kept both the hands under both the thighs, with the body straight, when one sits calmly in this posture, it is called Swastika.
sourceNotes: Sinh’s English says “hands”; the Sanskrit pāda-tale ubhe means “both soles”. The editorial draft follows the Sanskrit. The historical wording is retained with attribution.

iast:
savye dakṣiṇa-gulphaṃ tu pṛṣṭha-pārśve niyojayet  /
dakṣiṇe'pi tathā savyaṃ gomukhaṃ gomukhākṛtiḥ
devanagari:
सव्ये दक्षिण-गुल्फं तु पृष्ठ-पार्श्वे नियोजयेत्  ।
दक्षिणेऽपि तथा सव्यं गोमुखं गोमुखाकृतिः
english: Placing the right ankle on the left side and the left ankle on the right side, makes Gomukha-âsana, having the appearance of a cow.
sourceNotes: Sanskrit Documents has gulkaṃ where GRETIL has gulphaṃ (ankle). This is a transcription difference; the atlas retains its named GRETIL base.

iast:
ekaṃ pādaṃ tathaikasmin vinyased uruṇi sthiram  /
itarasmiṃs tathā coruṃ vīrāsanam itīritam
devanagari:
एकं पादं तथैकस्मिन् विन्यसेद् उरुणि स्थिरम्  ।
इतरस्मिंस् तथा चोरुं वीरासनम् इतीरितम्
english: One foot is to be placed on the thigh of the opposite side; and so also the other foot on the opposite thigh. This is called Vîrâsana.

iast:
gudaṃ nirudhya gulphābhyāṃ vyutkrameṇa samāhitaḥ  /
kūrmāsanaṃ bhaved etad iti yoga-vido viduḥ
devanagari:
गुदं निरुध्य गुल्फाभ्यां व्युत्क्रमेण समाहितः  ।
कूर्मासनं भवेद् एतद् इति योग-विदो विदुः
english: Placing the right ankle on the left side of anus, and the left ankle on the right side of it, makes what the Yogîs call Kûrma-âsana.

iast:
padmāsanaṃ tu saṃsthāpya jānūrvor antare karau  /
niveśya bhūmau saṃsthāpya vyomasthaṃ kukkuṭāsanam
devanagari:
पद्मासनं तु संस्थाप्य जानूर्वोर् अन्तरे करौ  ।
निवेश्य भूमौ संस्थाप्य व्योमस्थं कुक्कुटासनम्
english: Taking the posture of Padma-âsana and carrying the hands under the thighs, when the Yogî raises himself above the ground, with his palms resting on the ground, it becomes Kukkuṭa-âsana.

iast:
kukkuṭāsana-bandha-stho dorbhyāṃ sambadya kandharām  /
bhaved kūrmavad uttāna etad uttāna-kūrmakam
devanagari:
कुक्कुटासन-बन्ध-स्थो दोर्भ्यां सम्बद्य कन्धराम्  ।
भवेद् कूर्मवद् उत्तान एतद् उत्तान-कूर्मकम्
english: Having assumed Kukkuṭa-âsana, when one grasps his neck by crossing his hands behind his head, and lies in this posture with his back touching the ground, it becomes Uttâna Kûrma-âsana, from its appearance like that of a tortoise.

iast:
pādāṅguṣṭhau tu pāṇibhyāṃ gṛhītvā śravaṇāvadhi  /
dhanur ākarṣaṇaṃ kuryād dhanur-āsanam ucyate
devanagari:
पादाङ्गुष्ठौ तु पाणिभ्यां गृहीत्वा श्रवणावधि  ।
धनुर् आकर्षणं कुर्याद् धनुर्-आसनम् उच्यते
english: Having caught the toes of the feet with both the hands and carried them to the ears by drawing the body like a bow, it becomes Dhanura âsana.

iast:
vāmoru-mūlārpita-dakṣa-pādaṃ
jānor bahir veṣṭita-vāma-pādam  /
pragṛhya tiṣṭhet parivartitāṅgaḥ
śrī-matysanāthoditam āsanaṃ syāt
devanagari:
वामोरु-मूलार्पित-दक्ष-पादं
जानोर् बहिर् वेष्टित-वाम-पादम्  ।
प्रगृह्य तिष्ठेत् परिवर्तिताङ्गः
श्री-मत्य्सनाथोदितम् आसनं स्यात्
english: Having placed the right foot at the root of the left thigh, let the toe be grasped with the right hand passing over the back, and having placed the left foot on the right thigh at its root, let it be grasped with the left hand passing behind the back. This is the âsana, as explained by Śri Matsyanâtha. It increases appetite and is an instrument for destroying the group of the most deadly diseases. Its practice awakens the Kundalinî, stops the nectar shedding from the moon in people.
translationNote: English and Sanskrit numbering/segmentation differ in the Sinh digitization; the translation is cross-referenced by content. A shared translation may cover more than one verse.

iast:
matsyendra-pīṭhaṃ jaṭhara-pradīptiṃ
pracaṇḍa-rug maṇḍala-khaṇḍanāstram  /
abhyāsataḥ kuṇḍalinī-prabodhaṃ
candra-sthiratvaṃ ca dadāti puṃsām
devanagari:
मत्स्येन्द्र-पीठं जठर-प्रदीप्तिं
प्रचण्ड-रुग् मण्डल-खण्डनास्त्रम्  ।
अभ्यासतः कुण्डलिनी-प्रबोधं
चन्द्र-स्थिरत्वं च ददाति पुंसाम्
english: Having placed the right foot at the root of the left thigh, let the toe be grasped with the right hand passing over the back, and having placed the left foot on the right thigh at its root, let it be grasped with the left hand passing behind the back. This is the âsana, as explained by Śri Matsyanâtha. It increases appetite and is an instrument for destroying the group of the most deadly diseases. Its practice awakens the Kundalinî, stops the nectar shedding from the moon in people.
translationNote: English and Sanskrit numbering/segmentation differ in the Sinh digitization; the translation is cross-referenced by content. A shared translation may cover more than one verse.

iast:
prasārya pādau bhuvi daṇḍa-rūpau
dorbhyāṃ padāgra-dvitayaṃ gṛhītvā  /
jānūparinyasta-lalāṭa-deśo
vased idaṃ paścimatānam āhuḥ
devanagari:
प्रसार्य पादौ भुवि दण्ड-रूपौ
दोर्भ्यां पदाग्र-द्वितयं गृहीत्वा  ।
जानूपरिन्यस्त-ललाट-देशो
वसेद् इदं पश्चिमतानम् आहुः
english: Having stretched the feet on the ground, like a stick, and having grasped the toes of both the feet with both the hands, when one sits with his forehead resting on the thighs, it is called Paśchima Tâna.

iast:
iti paścimatānam āsanāgryaṃ
pavanaṃ paścima-vāhinaṃ karoti  /
udayaṃ jaṭharānalasya kuryād
udare kārśyam arogatāṃ ca puṃsām
devanagari:
इति पश्चिमतानम् आसनाग्र्यं
पवनं पश्चिम-वाहिनं करोति  ।
उदयं जठरानलस्य कुर्याद्
उदरे कार्श्यम् अरोगतां च पुंसाम्
english: This Paśchima Tâna carries the air from the front to the back part of the body ( i.e. , to the suṣumna). It kindles gastric fire, reduces obesity and cures all diseases of men.

iast:
dharām avaṣṭabhya kara-dvayena
tat-kūrpara-sthāpita-nābhi-pārśvaḥ  /
uccāsano daṇḍavad utthitaḥ khe
māyūram etat pravadanti pīṭham
devanagari:
धराम् अवष्टभ्य कर-द्वयेन
तत्-कूर्पर-स्थापित-नाभि-पार्श्वः  ।
उच्चासनो दण्डवद् उत्थितः खे
मायूरम् एतत् प्रवदन्ति पीठम्
english: Place the palms of both the hands on the ground, and place the navel on both the elbows and balancing thus, the body should be stretched backward like a stick. This is called Mayûra-âsana.

iast:
harati sakala-rogān āśu gulmodarādīn
abhibhavati ca doṣān āsanaṃ śrī-mayūram  /
bahu kadaśana-bhuktaṃ bhasma kuryād aśeṣaṃ
janayati jaṭharāgniṃ jārayet kāla-kūṭam
devanagari:
हरति सकल-रोगान् आशु गुल्मोदरादीन्
अभिभवति च दोषान् आसनं श्री-मयूरम्  ।
बहु कदशन-भुक्तं भस्म कुर्याद् अशेषं
जनयति जठराग्निं जारयेत् काल-कूटम्
english: This Âsana soon destroys all diseases, and removes abdominal disorders, and also those arising from irregularities of phlegm, bile and wind, digests unwholesome food taken in excess, increases appetite and destroys the most deadly poison.

iast:
uttānaṃ śabavad bhūmau śayanaṃ tac chavāsanam  /
śavāsanaṃ śrānti-haraṃ citta-viśrānti-kārakam
devanagari:
उत्तानं शबवद् भूमौ शयनं तच् छवासनम्  ।
शवासनं श्रान्ति-हरं चित्त-विश्रान्ति-कारकम्
english: Lying down on the ground, like a corpse, is called Śava-âsana. It removes fatigue and gives rest to the mind.
sourceNotes: Source reads śabavad; the expected reading is śavavad (śava-vat, like a corpse). The diplomatic source spelling is retained.

iast:
caturaśīty āsanāni śivena kathitāni ca  /
tebhyaś catuṣkam ādāya sārabhūtaṃ bravīmy aham
devanagari:
चतुरशीत्य् आसनानि शिवेन कथितानि च  ।
तेभ्यश् चतुष्कम् आदाय सारभूतं ब्रवीम्य् अहम्
english: Śiva taught 84 âsanas. Of these the first four being essential ones, I am going to explain them here.

iast:
siddhaṃ padmaṃ tathā siṃhaṃ bhadraṃ veti catuṣṭayam  /
śreṣṭhaṃ tatrāpi ca sukhe tiṣṭhet siddhāsane sadā
devanagari:
सिद्धं पद्मं तथा सिंहं भद्रं वेति चतुष्टयम्  ।
श्रेष्ठं तत्रापि च सुखे तिष्ठेत् सिद्धासने सदा
english: These four are:—The Siddha, Padma, Sinha and Bhadra. Even of these, the Siddha-âsana, being very comfortable, one should always practise it.

iast:
yoni-sthānakam aṅghri-mūla-ghaṭitaṃ kṛtvā dṛḍhaṃ vinyaset
meṇḍhre pādam athaikam eva hṛdaye kṛtvā hanuṃ susthiram  /
sthāṇuḥ saṃyamitendriyo'cala-dṛśā paśyed bhruvor antaraṃ
hy etan mokṣa-kapāṭa-bheda-janakaṃ siddhāsanaṃ procyate
devanagari:
योनि-स्थानकम् अङ्घ्रि-मूल-घटितं कृत्वा दृढं विन्यसेत्
मेण्ढ्रे पादम् अथैकम् एव हृदये कृत्वा हनुं सुस्थिरम्  ।
स्थाणुः संयमितेन्द्रियोऽचल-दृशा पश्येद् भ्रुवोर् अन्तरं
ह्य् एतन् मोक्ष-कपाट-भेद-जनकं सिद्धासनं प्रोच्यते
english: Press firmly the heel of the left foot against the perineum, and the right heel above the male organ. With the chin pressing on the chest, one should sit calmly, having restrained the senses, and gaze steadily the space between the eyebrows. This is called the Siddha Âsana, the opener of the door of salvation.

iast:
meṇḍhrād upari vinyasya savyaṃ gulphaṃ tathopari  /
gulphāntaraṃ ca nikṣipya siddhāsanam idaṃ bhavet
devanagari:
मेण्ढ्राद् उपरि विन्यस्य सव्यं गुल्फं तथोपरि  ।
गुल्फान्तरं च निक्षिप्य सिद्धासनम् इदं भवेत्
english: This Siddhâsana is performed also by placing the left heel on Meḍhra (above the male organ), and then placing the right one on it.

iast:
etat siddhāsanaṃ prāhur anye vajrāsanaṃ viduḥ  /
muktāsanaṃ vadanty eke prāhur guptāsanaṃ pare
devanagari:
एतत् सिद्धासनं प्राहुर् अन्ये वज्रासनं विदुः  ।
मुक्तासनं वदन्त्य् एके प्राहुर् गुप्तासनं परे
english: Some call this Siddhâsana, some Vajrâsana. Others call it Mukta Âsana or Gupta Âsana.

iast:
yameṣv iva mitāhāram ahiṃsā niyameṣv iva  /
mukhyaṃ sarvāsaneṣv ekaṃ siddhāḥ siddhāsanaṃ viduḥ
devanagari:
यमेष्व् इव मिताहारम् अहिंसा नियमेष्व् इव  ।
मुख्यं सर्वासनेष्व् एकं सिद्धाः सिद्धासनं विदुः
english: Just as sparing food is among Yamas, and Ahiṃsâ among the Niyamas, so is Siddhâsana called by adepts the chief of all the âsanas.

iast:
caturaśīti-pīṭheṣu siddham eva sadābhyaset  /
dvāsaptati-sahasrāṇāṃ nāḍīnāṃ mala-śodhanam
devanagari:
चतुरशीति-पीठेषु सिद्धम् एव सदाभ्यसेत्  ।
द्वासप्तति-सहस्राणां नाडीनां मल-शोधनम्
english: Out of the 84 Âsanas Siddhâsana should always be practised, because it cleanses the impurities of 72,000 nâḍîs.

iast:
ātma-dhyāyī mitāhārī yāvad dvādaśa-vatsaram  /
sadā siddhāsanābhyāsād yogī niṣpattim āpnuyāt
devanagari:
आत्म-ध्यायी मिताहारी यावद् द्वादश-वत्सरम्  ।
सदा सिद्धासनाभ्यासाद् योगी निष्पत्तिम् आप्नुयात्
english: By contemplating on oneself, by eating sparingly, and by practising Siddhâsana for 12 years, the Yogî obtains success.

iast:
kim anyair bahubhiḥ pīṭhaiḥ siddhe siddhāsane sati  /
prāṇānile sāvadhāne baddhe kevala-kumbhake  /
utpadyate nirāyāsāt svayam evonmanī kalā
devanagari:
किम् अन्यैर् बहुभिः पीठैः सिद्धे सिद्धासने सति  ।
प्राणानिले सावधाने बद्धे केवल-कुम्भके  ।
उत्पद्यते निरायासात् स्वयम् एवोन्मनी कला
english: Other postures are of no use, when success has been achieved in Siddhâsana, and Prâṇa Vâyû becomes calm and restrained by Kevala Kumbhaka.

iast:
tathaikāsminn eva dṛḍhe siddhe siddhāsane sati  /
bandha-trayam anāyāsāt svayam evopajāyate
devanagari:
तथैकास्मिन्न् एव दृढे सिद्धे सिद्धासने सति  ।
बन्ध-त्रयम् अनायासात् स्वयम् एवोपजायते
english: Success in one Siddhâsana alone becoming firmly established, one gets Unmanî at once, and the three bonds (Bandhas) are accomplished of themselves.

iast:
nāsanaṃ siddha-sadṛśaṃ na kumbhaḥ kevalopamaḥ  /
na khecarī-samā mudrā na nāda-sadṛśo layaḥ
devanagari:
नासनं सिद्ध-सदृशं न कुम्भः केवलोपमः  ।
न खेचरी-समा मुद्रा न नाद-सदृशो लयः
english: There is no Âsana like the Siddhâsana and no Kumbhaka like the Kevala. There is no mudrâ like the Khechari and no laya like the Nâda (Anâhata Nâda.)

iast:
vāmorūpari dakṣiṇaṃ ca caraṇaṃ saṃsthāpya vāmaṃ tathā
dakṣorūpari paścimena vidhinā dhṛtvā karābhyāṃ dṛḍham  /
aṅguṣṭhau hṛdaye nidhāya cibukaṃ nāsāgram ālokayet
etad vyādhi-vināśa-kāri yamināṃ padmāsanaṃ procyate
devanagari:
वामोरूपरि दक्षिणं च चरणं संस्थाप्य वामं तथा
दक्षोरूपरि पश्चिमेन विधिना धृत्वा कराभ्यां दृढम्  ।
अङ्गुष्ठौ हृदये निधाय चिबुकं नासाग्रम् आलोकयेत्
एतद् व्याधि-विनाश-कारि यमिनां पद्मासनं प्रोच्यते
english: Place the right foot on the left thigh and the left foot on the right thigh, and grasp the toes with the hands crossed over the back. Press the chin against the chest and gaze on the tip of the nose. This is called the Padmâsana, the destroyer of the diseases of the Yamîs.

iast:
uttānau caraṇau kṛtvā ūru-saṃsthau prayatnataḥ  /
ūru-madhye tathottānau pāṇī kṛtvā tato dṛśau
devanagari:
उत्तानौ चरणौ कृत्वा ऊरु-संस्थौ प्रयत्नतः  ।
ऊरु-मध्ये तथोत्तानौ पाणी कृत्वा ततो दृशौ
english: Place the feet on the thighs, with the soles upwards, and place the hands on the thighs, with the palms upwards.

iast:
nāsāgre vinyased rājad-anta-mūle tu jihvayā  /
uttambhya cibukaṃ vakṣasy utthāpy pavanaṃ śanaiḥ
devanagari:
नासाग्रे विन्यसेद् राजद्-अन्त-मूले तु जिह्वया  ।
उत्तम्भ्य चिबुकं वक्षस्य् उत्थाप्य् पवनं शनैः
english: Gaze on the tip of the nose, keeping the tongue pressed against the root of the teeth of the upper jaw, and the chin against the chest, and raise the air up slowly, i.e. , pull the apâna-vâyû gently upwards.

iast:
idaṃ padmāsanaṃ proktaṃ sarva-vyādhi-vināśanam  /
durlabhaṃ yena kenāpi dhīmatā labhyate bhuvi
devanagari:
इदं पद्मासनं प्रोक्तं सर्व-व्याधि-विनाशनम्  ।
दुर्लभं येन केनापि धीमता लभ्यते भुवि
english: This is called the Padmâsana, the destroyer of all diseases. It is difficult of attainment by everybody, but can be learnt by intelligent people in this world.

iast:
kṛtvā sampuṭitau karau dṛḍhataraṃ baddhvā tu padmāsanaṃ
gāḍhaṃ vakṣasi sannidhāya cibukaṃ dhyāyaṃś ca tac cetasi  /
vāraṃ vāram apānam ūrdhvam anilaṃ protsārayan pūritaṃ
nyañcan prāṇam upaiti bodham atulaṃ śakti-prabhāvān naraḥ
devanagari:
कृत्वा सम्पुटितौ करौ दृढतरं बद्ध्वा तु पद्मासनं
गाढं वक्षसि सन्निधाय चिबुकं ध्यायंश् च तच् चेतसि  ।
वारं वारम् अपानम् ऊर्ध्वम् अनिलं प्रोत्सारयन् पूरितं
न्यञ्चन् प्राणम् उपैति बोधम् अतुलं शक्ति-प्रभावान् नरः
english: Having kept both the hands together in the lap, performing the Padmâsana firmly, keeping the chin Fixed to the chest and contemplating on Him in the mind, by drawing the apâna-vâyû up (performing Mûla Bandha) and pushing down the air after inhaling it, joining thus the prâṇa and apâna in the navel, one gets the highest intelligence by awakening the śakti (kundalinî) thus.
sourceNotes: Sanskrit Documents has padmamāsanaṃ against GRETIL padmāsanaṃ. The extra syllable is not imported into the base text.

iast:
padmāsane sthito yogī nāḍī-dvāreṇa pūritam  /
mārutaṃ dhārayed yas tu sa mukto nātra saṃśayaḥ
devanagari:
पद्मासने स्थितो योगी नाडी-द्वारेण पूरितम्  ।
मारुतं धारयेद् यस् तु स मुक्तो नात्र संशयः
english: The Yogî who, sitting with Padmâsana, can control breathing, there is no doubt, is free from bondage.

iast:
gulphau ca vṛṣaṇasyādhaḥ sīvanyāḥ pārśvayoḥ kṣipet  /
dakṣiṇe savya-gulphaṃ tu dakṣa-gulphaṃ tu savyake
devanagari:
गुल्फौ च वृषणस्याधः सीवन्याः पार्श्वयोः क्षिपेत्  ।
दक्षिणे सव्य-गुल्फं तु दक्ष-गुल्फं तु सव्यके
english: Press the heels on both sides of the seam of Perineum, in such a way that the left heel touches the right side and the right heel touches the left side of it.
sourceNotes: Sanskrit Documents has sīvantyāḥ against GRETIL sīvanyāḥ; compare the same difference at 1.55. Both displays need to be distinguished from independent manuscript evidence.

iast:
hastau tu jānvoḥ saṃsthāpya svāṅgulīḥ samprasārya ca  /
vyātta-vaktro nirīkṣeta nāsāgraṃ susamāhitaḥ
devanagari:
हस्तौ तु जान्वोः संस्थाप्य स्वाङ्गुलीः सम्प्रसार्य च  ।
व्यात्त-वक्त्रो निरीक्षेत नासाग्रं सुसमाहितः
english: Place the hands on the thighs, with stretched fingers, and keeping the mouth open and the mind collected, gaze on the tip of the nose.
sourceNotes: Sanskrit Documents has vyātta-vakto where GRETIL has vyātta-vaktro (with mouth open). The atlas retains the GRETIL reading.

iast:
siṃhāsanaṃ bhaved etat pūjitaṃ yogi-puṅgavaiḥ  /
bandha-tritaya-sandhānaṃ kurute cāsanottamam
devanagari:
सिंहासनं भवेद् एतत् पूजितं योगि-पुङ्गवैः  ।
बन्ध-त्रितय-सन्धानं कुरुते चासनोत्तमम्
english: This is Siṃhâsana, held sacred by the best of Yogîs. This excellent Âsana effects the completion of the three Bandhas (The Mûlabandha, Kanṭha or Jâlandhar Bandha and Uḍḍiyâna Bandha).

iast:
gulphau ca vṛṣaṇasyādhaḥ sīvanyāḥ pārśvayoḥ kṣipte  /
savya-gulphaṃ tathā savye dakṣa-gulphaṃ tu dakṣiṇe
devanagari:
गुल्फौ च वृषणस्याधः सीवन्याः पार्श्वयोः क्षिप्ते  ।
सव्य-गुल्फं तथा सव्ये दक्ष-गुल्फं तु दक्षिणे
english: Place the heels on either side of the seam of the Perineum, keeping the left heel on the left side and the right one on the right side, hold the feet firmly joined to one another with both the hands. This Bhadrâsana is the destroyer of all the diseases.
translationNote: English and Sanskrit numbering/segmentation differ in the Sinh digitization; the translation is cross-referenced by content. A shared translation may cover more than one verse.
sourceNotes: Sanskrit Documents has sīvantyāḥ against GRETIL sīvanyāḥ. The Sinh English 55–57 crosses the Sanskrit 55–57 boundaries; shared text is repeated with its full English reference numbers.

iast:
pārśva-pādau ca pāṇibhyāṃ dṛḍhaṃ baddhvā suniścalam  /
bhadrāsanaṃ bhaved etat sarva-vyādhi-vināśanam  /
gorakṣāsanam ity āhur idaṃ vai siddha-yoginaḥ
devanagari:
पार्श्व-पादौ च पाणिभ्यां दृढं बद्ध्वा सुनिश्चलम्  ।
भद्रासनं भवेद् एतत् सर्व-व्याधि-विनाशनम्  ।
गोरक्षासनम् इत्य् आहुर् इदं वै सिद्ध-योगिनः
english: Place the heels on either side of the seam of the Perineum, keeping the left heel on the left side and the right one on the right side, hold the feet firmly joined to one another with both the hands. This Bhadrâsana is the destroyer of all the diseases. The expert Yogîs call this Gorakśa âsana. By sitting with this âsana, the Yogî gets rid of fatigue
translationNote: English and Sanskrit numbering/segmentation differ in the Sinh digitization; the translation is cross-referenced by content. A shared translation may cover more than one verse.

iast:
evam āsana-bandheṣu yogīndro vigata-śramaḥ  /
abhyasen nāḍikā-śuddhiṃ mudrādi-pavanī-kriyām
devanagari:
एवम् आसन-बन्धेषु योगीन्द्रो विगत-श्रमः  ।
अभ्यसेन् नाडिका-शुद्धिं मुद्रादि-पवनी-क्रियाम्
english: The expert Yogîs call this Gorakśa âsana. By sitting with this âsana, the Yogî gets rid of fatigue The Nâdis should be cleansed of their impurities by performing the mudrâs, etc., (which are the practices relating to the air) Âsanas, Kumbhakas and various curious mûdrâs.
translationNote: English and Sanskrit numbering/segmentation differ in the Sinh digitization; the translation is cross-referenced by content. A shared translation may cover more than one verse.

iast:
āsanaṃ kumbhakaṃ citraṃ mudrākhyaṃ karaṇaṃ tathā  /
atha nādānusandhānam abhyāsānukramo haṭhe
devanagari:
आसनं कुम्भकं चित्रं मुद्राख्यं करणं तथा  ।
अथ नादानुसन्धानम् अभ्यासानुक्रमो हठे
english: The Nâdis should be cleansed of their impurities by performing the mudrâs, etc., (which are the practices relating to the air) Âsanas, Kumbhakas and various curious mûdrâs.
translationNote: English and Sanskrit numbering/segmentation differ in the Sinh digitization; the translation is cross-referenced by content. A shared translation may cover more than one verse.

iast:
brahmacārī mitāhārī tyāgī yoga-parāyaṇaḥ  /
abdād ūrdhvaṃ bhavet siddho nātra kāryā vicāraṇā
devanagari:
ब्रह्मचारी मिताहारी त्यागी योग-परायणः  ।
अब्दाद् ऊर्ध्वं भवेत् सिद्धो नात्र कार्या विचारणा
english: By regular and close attention to Nâda (anâhata nâda) in Haṭha Yoga, a Brahmachari, sparing in diet, unattached to objects of enjoyment, and devoted to Yoga, gains success, no doubt, within a year.
sourceNotes: Sanskrit Documents has bhavedsiddho against GRETIL bhavet siddho. This is a consonant-sandhi/spelling difference; the named GRETIL source is preserved.

iast:
susnigdha-madhurāhāraś caturthāṃśa-vivarjitaḥ  /
bhujyate śiva-samprītyai mitāhāraḥ sa ucyate
devanagari:
सुस्निग्ध-मधुराहारश् चतुर्थांश-विवर्जितः  ।
भुज्यते शिव-सम्प्रीत्यै मिताहारः स उच्यते
english: Abstemious feeding is that in which ¾ of hunger is satisfied with food, well cooked with ghee and sweets, and eaten with the offering of it to Śiva.

iast:
kaṭvāmla-tīkṣṇa-lavaṇoṣṇa-harīta-śāka-
sauvīra-taila-tila-sarṣapa-madya-matsyān  /
ājādi-māṃsa-dadhi-takra-kulatthakola-
piṇyāka-hiṅgu-laśunādyam apathyam āhuḥ
devanagari:
कट्वाम्ल-तीक्ष्ण-लवणोष्ण-हरीत-शाक-
सौवीर-तैल-तिल-सर्षप-मद्य-मत्स्यान्  ।
आजादि-मांस-दधि-तक्र-कुलत्थकोल-
पिण्याक-हिङ्गु-लशुनाद्यम् अपथ्यम् आहुः
english: Bitter, sour, saltish, hot, green vegetables, fermented, oily, mixed with til seed, rape seed, intoxicating liquors, fish, meat, curds, chhaasa pulses, plums, oil-cake, asafœtida (hînga), garlic, onion, etc., should not be eaten.

iast:
bhojanam ahitaṃ vidyāt punar asyoṣṇī-kṛtaṃ rūkṣam  /
atilavaṇam amla-yuktaṃ kadaśana-śākotkaṃ varjyam
devanagari:
भोजनम् अहितं विद्यात् पुनर् अस्योष्णी-कृतं रूक्षम्  ।
अतिलवणम् अम्ल-युक्तं कदशन-शाकोत्कं वर्ज्यम्
english: Food heated again, dry, having too much salt, sour, minor grains, and vegetables that cause burning sensation, should not be eaten, Fire, women, travelling, etc., should be avoided.
translationNote: English and Sanskrit numbering/segmentation differ in the Sinh digitization; the translation is cross-referenced by content. A shared translation may cover more than one verse.

iast: vahni-strī-pathi-sevānām ādau varjanam ācaret
devanagari: वह्नि-स्त्री-पथि-सेवानाम् आदौ वर्जनम् आचरेत्
english: Food heated again, dry, having too much salt, sour, minor grains, and vegetables that cause burning sensation, should not be eaten, Fire, women, travelling, etc., should be avoided.
translationNote: English and Sanskrit numbering/segmentation differ in the Sinh digitization; the translation is cross-referenced by content. A shared translation may cover more than one verse.

iast:
varjayed durjana-prāntaṃ vahni-strī-pathi-sevanam  /
prātaḥ-snānopavāsādi kāya-kleśa-vidhiṃ tathā
devanagari:
वर्जयेद् दुर्जन-प्रान्तं वह्नि-स्त्री-पथि-सेवनम्  ।
प्रातः-स्नानोपवासादि काय-क्लेश-विधिं तथा
english: As said by Gorakṣa, one should keep aloof from the society of the evil-minded, fire, women, travelling, early morning bath, fasting, and all kinds of bodily exertion.
translationNote: English and Sanskrit numbering/segmentation differ in the Sinh digitization; the translation is cross-referenced by content. A shared translation may cover more than one verse.

iast:
godhūma-śāli-yava-ṣāṣṭika-śobhanānnaṃ
kṣīrājya-khaṇḍa-navanīta-siddhā-madhūni  /
śuṇṭhī-paṭola-kaphalādika-pañca-śākaṃ
mudgādi-divyam udakaṃ ca yamīndra-pathyam
devanagari:
गोधूम-शालि-यव-षाष्टिक-शोभनान्नं
क्षीराज्य-खण्ड-नवनीत-सिद्धा-मधूनि  ।
शुण्ठी-पटोल-कफलादिक-पञ्च-शाकं
मुद्गादि-दिव्यम् उदकं च यमीन्द्र-पथ्यम्
english: Wheat, rice, barley, shâstik (a kind of rice), good corns, milk, ghee, sugar, butter, sugarcandy, honey, dried ginger, Parwal (a vegetable) the five vegetables, moong, pure water, these are very beneficial to those who practise Yoga.
translationNote: English and Sanskrit numbering/segmentation differ in the Sinh digitization; the translation is cross-referenced by content. A shared translation may cover more than one verse.

iast:
puṣṭaṃ sumadhuraṃ snigdhaṃ gavyaṃ dhātu-prapoṣaṇam  /
manobhilaṣitaṃ yogyaṃ yogī bhojanam ācaret
devanagari:
पुष्टं सुमधुरं स्निग्धं गव्यं धातु-प्रपोषणम्  ।
मनोभिलषितं योग्यं योगी भोजनम् आचरेत्
english: A Yogî should eat tonics (things giving strength), well sweetened, greasy (made with ghee), milk, butter, etc., which may increase humors of the body, according to his desire.
translationNote: English and Sanskrit numbering/segmentation differ in the Sinh digitization; the translation is cross-referenced by content. A shared translation may cover more than one verse.

iast:
yuvo vṛddho'tivṛddho vā vyādhito durbalo'pi vā  /
abhyāsāt siddhim āpnoti sarva-yogeṣv atandritaḥ
devanagari:
युवो वृद्धोऽतिवृद्धो वा व्याधितो दुर्बलोऽपि वा  ।
अभ्यासात् सिद्धिम् आप्नोति सर्व-योगेष्व् अतन्द्रितः
english: Whether young, old or too old, sick or lean, one who discards laziness, gets success if he practises Yoga.
translationNote: English and Sanskrit numbering/segmentation differ in the Sinh digitization; the translation is cross-referenced by content. A shared translation may cover more than one verse.

iast:
kriyā-yuktasya siddhiḥ syād akriyasya kathaṃ bhavet  /
na śāstra-pāṭha-mātreṇa yoga-siddhiḥ prajāyate
devanagari:
क्रिया-युक्तस्य सिद्धिः स्याद् अक्रियस्य कथं भवेत्  ।
न शास्त्र-पाठ-मात्रेण योग-सिद्धिः प्रजायते
english: Success comes to him who is engaged in the practice. How can one get success without practice; for by merely reading books on Yoga, one can never get success.
translationNote: English and Sanskrit numbering/segmentation differ in the Sinh digitization; the translation is cross-referenced by content. A shared translation may cover more than one verse.

iast:
na veṣa-dhāraṇaṃ siddheḥ kāraṇaṃ na ca tat-kathā  /
kriyaiva kāraṇaṃ siddheḥ satyam etan na saṃśayaḥ
devanagari:
न वेष-धारणं सिद्धेः कारणं न च तत्-कथा  ।
क्रियैव कारणं सिद्धेः सत्यम् एतन् न संशयः
english: Success cannot be attained by adopting a particular dress (Veṣa). It cannot be gained by telling tales. Practice alone is the means to success. This is true, there is no doubt.
translationNote: English and Sanskrit numbering/segmentation differ in the Sinh digitization; the translation is cross-referenced by content. A shared translation may cover more than one verse.

iast:
pīṭhāni kumbhakāś citrā divyāni karaṇāni ca  /
sarvāṇy api haṭhābhyāse rāja-yoga-phalāvadhi
devanagari:
पीठानि कुम्भकाश् चित्रा दिव्यानि करणानि च  ।
सर्वाण्य् अपि हठाभ्यासे राज-योग-फलावधि
english: Âsanas (postures), various Kumbhakas, and other divine means, all should be practised in the practice of Haṭha Yoga, till the fruit—Râja Yoga—is obtained.
translationNote: English and Sanskrit numbering/segmentation differ in the Sinh digitization; the translation is cross-referenced by content. A shared translation may cover more than one verse.

iast:
athāsane dṛdhe yogī vaśī hita-mitāśanaḥ  /
gurūpadiṣṭa-mārgeṇa prāṇāyāmān samabhyaset
devanagari:
अथासने दृधे योगी वशी हित-मिताशनः  ।
गुरूपदिष्ट-मार्गेण प्राणायामान् समभ्यसेत्
english: Posture becoming established, a Yogî, master of himself, eating salutary and moderate food, should practise Prâṇâyâma, as instructed by his guru.
sourceNotes: Source reads dṛdhe; expected dṛḍhe. The diplomatic source spelling is retained.

iast:
cale vāte calaṃ cittaṃ niścale niścalaṃ bhavet  /
yogī sthāṇutvam āpnoti tato vāyuṃ nirodhayet
devanagari:
चले वाते चलं चित्तं निश्चले निश्चलं भवेत्  ।
योगी स्थाणुत्वम् आप्नोति ततो वायुं निरोधयेत्
english: Respiration being disturbed, the mind becomes disturbed. By restraining respiration, the Yogî gets steadiness of mind
sourceNotes: A stray incomplete HYP_2. reference label in the source has been removed from the verse display.

iast:
yāvad vāyuḥ sthito dehe tāvaj jīvanam ucyate  /
maraṇaṃ tasya niṣkrāntis tato vāyuṃ nirodhayet
devanagari:
यावद् वायुः स्थितो देहे तावज् जीवनम् उच्यते  ।
मरणं तस्य निष्क्रान्तिस् ततो वायुं निरोधयेत्
english: So long as the (breathing) air stays in the body, it is called life. Death consists in the passing out of the (breathing) air. It is, therefore, necessary to restrain the breath.

iast:
malākalāsu nāḍīṣu māruto naiva madhyagaḥ  /
kathaṃ syād unmanībhāvaḥ kārya-siddhiḥ kathaṃ bhavet
devanagari:
मलाकलासु नाडीषु मारुतो नैव मध्यगः  ।
कथं स्याद् उन्मनीभावः कार्य-सिद्धिः कथं भवेत्
english: The breath does not pass through the middle channel (suṣumnâ), owing to the impurities of the nâdîs. How can then success be attained, and how can there be the unmanî avasthâ.

iast:
śuddham eti yadā sarvaṃ nāḍī-cakraṃ malākulam  /
tadaiva jāyate yogī prāṇa-saṃgrahaṇe kṣamaḥ
devanagari:
शुद्धम् एति यदा सर्वं नाडी-चक्रं मलाकुलम्  ।
तदैव जायते योगी प्राण-संग्रहणे क्षमः
english: When the whole system of nâdîs which is full of impurities, is cleaned, then the Yogî becomes able to control the Prâṇa.

iast:
prāṇāyāmaṃ tataḥ kuryān nityaṃ sāttvikayā dhiyā  /
yathā suṣumṇā-nāḍīsthā malāḥ śuddhiṃ prayānti ca
devanagari:
प्राणायामं ततः कुर्यान् नित्यं सात्त्विकया धिया  ।
यथा सुषुम्णा-नाडीस्था मलाः शुद्धिं प्रयान्ति च
english: Therefore, Prâṇâyâma should be performed daily with sâtwika buddhi (intellect free from raja and tama or activity and sloth), in order to drive out the impurities of the suṣumnâ.

iast:
baddha-padmāsano yogī prāṇaṃ candreṇa pūrayet  /
dhārayitvā yathā-śakti bhūyaḥ sūryeṇa recayet
devanagari:
बद्ध-पद्मासनो योगी प्राणं चन्द्रेण पूरयेत्  ।
धारयित्वा यथा-शक्ति भूयः सूर्येण रेचयेत्
english: Sitting in the Padmâsana posture the Yogî should fill in the air through the left nostril (closing the right one); and, keeping it confined according to one's ability, it should be expelled slowly through the sûrya (right nostril). Then, drawing in the air through the sûrya (right nostril) slowly, the belly should be filled, and after performing Kumbhaka as before, it should be expelled slowly through the chandra (left nostril).
translationNote: English and Sanskrit numbering/segmentation differ in the Sinh digitization; the translation is cross-referenced by content. A shared translation may cover more than one verse.

iast:
prāṇaṃ sūryeṇa cākṛṣya pūrayed udaraṃ śanaiḥ  /
vidhivat kumbhakaṃ kṛtvā punaś candreṇa recayet
devanagari:
प्राणं सूर्येण चाकृष्य पूरयेद् उदरं शनैः  ।
विधिवत् कुम्भकं कृत्वा पुनश् चन्द्रेण रेचयेत्
english: Sitting in the Padmâsana posture the Yogî should fill in the air through the left nostril (closing the right one); and, keeping it confined according to one's ability, it should be expelled slowly through the sûrya (right nostril). Then, drawing in the air through the sûrya (right nostril) slowly, the belly should be filled, and after performing Kumbhaka as before, it should be expelled slowly through the chandra (left nostril).
translationNote: English and Sanskrit numbering/segmentation differ in the Sinh digitization; the translation is cross-referenced by content. A shared translation may cover more than one verse.

iast:
yena tyajet tena pītvā dhārayed atirodhataḥ  /
recayec ca tato'nyena śanair eva na vegataḥ
devanagari:
येन त्यजेत् तेन पीत्वा धारयेद् अतिरोधतः  ।
रेचयेच् च ततोऽन्येन शनैर् एव न वेगतः
english: Inhaling thus through the one, through which it was expelled, and having restrained it there, till possible, it should be exhaled through the other, slowly and not forcibly.

iast:
prāṇaṃ ced iḍayā piben niyamitaṃ bhūyo'nyathā recayet
pītvā piṅgalayā samīraṇam atho baddhvā tyajed vāmayā  /
sūrya-candramasor anena vidhinābhyāsaṃ sadā tanvatāṃ
śuddhā nāḍi-gaṇā bhavanti yamināṃ māsa-trayād ūrdhvataḥ
devanagari:
प्राणं चेद् इडया पिबेन् नियमितं भूयोऽन्यथा रेचयेत्
पीत्वा पिङ्गलया समीरणम् अथो बद्ध्वा त्यजेद् वामया  ।
सूर्य-चन्द्रमसोर् अनेन विधिनाभ्यासं सदा तन्वतां
शुद्धा नाडि-गणा भवन्ति यमिनां मास-त्रयाद् ऊर्ध्वतः
english: If the air be inhaled through the left nostril, it should be expelled again through the other, and filling it through the right nostril, confining it there, it should be expelled through the left nostril. By practising in this way, through the right and the left nostrils alternately, the whole of the collection of the nâdîs of the yamîs (practisers) becomes clean, i.e. , free from impurities, after 3 months and over.

iast:
prātar madhyandine sāyam ardha-rātre ca kumbhakān  /
śanair aśīti-paryantaṃ catur vāraṃ samabhyaset
devanagari:
प्रातर् मध्यन्दिने सायम् अर्ध-रात्रे च कुम्भकान्  ।
शनैर् अशीति-पर्यन्तं चतुर् वारं समभ्यसेत्
english: Kumbhakas should be performed gradually 4 times during day and night, i.e. , (morning, noon, evening and midnight), till the number of Kumbhakas for one time is 80 and for day and night together it is 320.

iast:
kanīyasi bhaved sveda kampo bhavati madhyame  /
uttame sthānam āpnoti tato vāyuṃ nibandhayet
devanagari:
कनीयसि भवेद् स्वेद कम्पो भवति मध्यमे  ।
उत्तमे स्थानम् आप्नोति ततो वायुं निबन्धयेत्
english: In the beginning there is perspiration, in the middle stage there is quivering, and in the last or the 3rd stage one obtains steadiness; and then the breath should be made steady or motionless.

iast:
jalena śrama-jātena gātra-mardanam ācaret  /
dṛḍhatā laghutā caiva tena gātrasya jāyate
devanagari:
जलेन श्रम-जातेन गात्र-मर्दनम् आचरेत्  ।
दृढता लघुता चैव तेन गात्रस्य जायते
english: The perspiration exuding from exertion of practice should be rubbed into the body (and not wiped), as by so doing the body becomes strong.

iast:
abhyāsa-kāle prathame śastaṃ kṣīrājya-bhojanam  /
tato'bhyāse  dṛḍhībhūte na tādṛṅ-niyama-grahaḥ
devanagari:
अभ्यास-काले प्रथमे शस्तं क्षीराज्य-भोजनम्  ।
ततोऽभ्यासे  दृढीभूते न तादृङ्-नियम-ग्रहः
english: During the first stage of practice the food consisting of milk and ghee is wholesome. When the practice becomes established, no such restriction is necessary.

iast:
yathā siṃho gajo vyāghro bhaved vaśyaḥ śanaiḥ śanaiḥ  /
tathaiva sevito vāyur anyathā hanti sādhakam
devanagari:
यथा सिंहो गजो व्याघ्रो भवेद् वश्यः शनैः शनैः  ।
तथैव सेवितो वायुर् अन्यथा हन्ति साधकम्
english: Just as lions, elephants and tigers are controlled by and by, so the breath is controlled by slow degrees, otherwise ( i.e. , by being hasty or using too much force) it kills the practiser himself.

iast:
prāṇāyāmena yuktena sarva-roga-kṣayo bhavet  /
ayuktābhyāsa-yogena sarva-roga-samudgamaḥ
devanagari:
प्राणायामेन युक्तेन सर्व-रोग-क्षयो भवेत्  ।
अयुक्ताभ्यास-योगेन सर्व-रोग-समुद्गमः
english: When Prâṇayama, etc., are performed properly, they eradicate all diseases; but an improper practice generates diseases.

iast:
hikkā śvāsaś ca kāsaś ca śiraḥ-karṇākṣi-vedanāḥ  /
bhavanti vividhāḥ rogāḥ pavanasya prakopataḥ
devanagari:
हिक्का श्वासश् च कासश् च शिरः-कर्णाक्षि-वेदनाः  ।
भवन्ति विविधाः रोगाः पवनस्य प्रकोपतः
english: Hiccough, asthma, cough, pain in the head, the ears, and the eyes; these and other various kinds of diseases are generated by the disturbance of the breath.

iast:
yuktaṃ yuktaṃ tyajed vāyuṃ yuktaṃ yuktaṃ ca pūrayet  /
yuktaṃ yuktaṃ ca badhnīyād evaṃ siddhim avāpnuyāt
devanagari:
युक्तं युक्तं त्यजेद् वायुं युक्तं युक्तं च पूरयेत्  ।
युक्तं युक्तं च बध्नीयाद् एवं सिद्धिम् अवाप्नुयात्
english: The air should be expelled with proper tact and should be filled in skilfully; and when it has been kept confined properly it brings success.

iast:
yadā tu nāḍī-śuddhiḥ syāt tathā cihnāni bāhyataḥ  /
kāyasya kṛśatā kāntis tadā jāyate niścitam
devanagari:
यदा तु नाडी-शुद्धिः स्यात् तथा चिह्नानि बाह्यतः  ।
कायस्य कृशता कान्तिस् तदा जायते निश्चितम्
english: When the nâdîs become free from impurities, and there appear the outward signs of success, such as lean body and glowing colour, then one should feel certain of success.

iast:
yatheṣṭaṃ dhāraṇaṃ vāyor analasya pradīpanam  /
nādābhivyaktir ārogyaṃ jāyate nāḍi-śodhanāt
devanagari:
यथेष्टं धारणं वायोर् अनलस्य प्रदीपनम्  ।
नादाभिव्यक्तिर् आरोग्यं जायते नाडि-शोधनात्
english: By removing the impurities, the air can be restrained, according to one's wish and the appetite is increased, the divine sound is awakened, and the body becomes healthy.

iast:
meda-śleṣmādhikaḥ pūrvaṃ ṣaṭ-karmāṇi samācaret  /
anyas tu nācaret tāni doṣāṇāṃ samabhāvataḥ
devanagari:
मेद-श्लेष्माधिकः पूर्वं षट्-कर्माणि समाचरेत्  ।
अन्यस् तु नाचरेत् तानि दोषाणां समभावतः
english: If there be excess of fat or phlegm in the body, the six kinds of kriyâs (duties) should be performed first. But others, not suffering from the excess of these, should not perform them.

iast:
dhautir bastis tathā netis trāṭakaṃ naulikaṃ tathā  /
kapāla-bhātiś caitāni ṣaṭ-karmāṇi pracakṣate
devanagari:
धौतिर् बस्तिस् तथा नेतिस् त्राटकं नौलिकं तथा  ।
कपाल-भातिश् चैतानि षट्-कर्माणि प्रचक्षते
english: The six kinds of duties are: Dhauti, Basti, Neti, Trâtaka, Nauti and Kapâla Bhâti. These are called the six actions वटूकमि

iast:
karma ṣaṭkam idaṃ gopyaṃ ghaṭa-śodhana-kārakam  /
vicitra-guṇa-sandhāya pūjyate yogi-puṅgavaiḥ
devanagari:
कर्म षट्कम् इदं गोप्यं घट-शोधन-कारकम्  ।
विचित्र-गुण-सन्धाय पूज्यते योगि-पुङ्गवैः
english: These six kinds of actions which cleanse the body should be kept secret. They produce extraordinary attributes and are performed with earnestness by the best of Yogîs.

iast:
catur-aṅgula-vistāraṃ hasta-pañca-daśāyatam  /
gurūpadiṣṭa-mārgeṇa siktaṃ vastraṃ śanair graset  /
punaḥ pratyāharec caitad uditaṃ dhauti-karma tat
devanagari:
चतुर्-अङ्गुल-विस्तारं हस्त-पञ्च-दशायतम्  ।
गुरूपदिष्ट-मार्गेण सिक्तं वस्त्रं शनैर् ग्रसेत्  ।
पुनः प्रत्याहरेच् चैतद् उदितं धौति-कर्म तत्
english: A strip of cloth, about 3 inches wide and 15 cubits long, is pushed in (swallowed), when moist with warm water, through the passage shown by the guru, and is taken out again. This is called Dhauti Karma.

iast:
kāsa-śvāsa-plīha-kuṣṭhaṃ kapharogāś ca viṃśatiḥ  /
dhauti-karma-prabhāveṇa prayānty eva na saṃśayaḥ
devanagari:
कास-श्वास-प्लीह-कुष्ठं कफरोगाश् च विंशतिः  ।
धौति-कर्म-प्रभावेण प्रयान्त्य् एव न संशयः
english: There is no doubt, that cough, asthma, enlargement of the spleen, leprosy, and 20 kinds of diseases born of phlegm, disappear by the practice of Dhauti Karma.

iast:
nābhi-daghna-jale pāyau nyasta-nālotkaṭāsanaḥ  /
ādhārākuñcanaṃ kuryāt kṣālanaṃ basti-karma tat
devanagari:
नाभि-दघ्न-जले पायौ न्यस्त-नालोत्कटासनः  ।
आधाराकुञ्चनं कुर्यात् क्षालनं बस्ति-कर्म तत्
english: Squatting in navel-deep water, and introducing a six inches long, smooth piece of ½ an inch diameter pipe, open at both ends, half inside the anus; it (anus) should he drawn up (contracted) and then expelled. This washing is called the Basti Karma.

iast:
gulma-plīhodaraṃ cāpi vāta-pitta-kaphodbhavāḥ  /
basti-karma-prabhāveṇa kṣīyante sakalāmayāḥ
devanagari:
गुल्म-प्लीहोदरं चापि वात-पित्त-कफोद्भवाः  ।
बस्ति-कर्म-प्रभावेण क्षीयन्ते सकलामयाः
english: By practising this Basti Karma, colic, enlarged spleen, and dropsy, arising from the disorders of Vâta (air), pitta (bile) and kapha (phlegm), are all cured.

iast:
dhāntvadriyāntaḥ-karaṇa-prasādaṃ
dadhāc ca kāntiṃ dahana-pradīptam  /
aśeṣa-doṣopacayaṃ nihanyād
abhyasyamānaṃ jala-basti-karma
devanagari:
धान्त्वद्रियान्तः-करण-प्रसादं
दधाच् च कान्तिं दहन-प्रदीप्तम्  ।
अशेष-दोषोपचयं निहन्याद्
अभ्यस्यमानं जल-बस्ति-कर्म
english: By practising Basti with water, the Dhâtâs, the Indriyas and the mind become calm. It gives glow and tone to the body and increases the appetite. All the disorders disappear.

iast:
sūtraṃ vitasti-susnigdhaṃ nāsānāle praveśayet  /
mukhān nirgamayec caiṣā netiḥ siddhair nigadyate
devanagari:
सूत्रं वितस्ति-सुस्निग्धं नासानाले प्रवेशयेत्  ।
मुखान् निर्गमयेच् चैषा नेतिः सिद्धैर् निगद्यते
english: A cord made of threads and about six inches long, should be passed through the passage of the nose and the end taken out in the mouth. This is called by adepts the Neti Karma.

iast:
kapāla-śodhinī caiva divya-dṛṣṭi-pradāyinī  /
jatrūrdhva-jāta-rogaughaṃ netir āśu nihanti ca
devanagari:
कपाल-शोधिनी चैव दिव्य-दृष्टि-प्रदायिनी  ।
जत्रूर्ध्व-जात-रोगौघं नेतिर् आशु निहन्ति च
english: The Neti is the cleaner of the brain and giver of divine sight. It soon destroys all the diseases of the cervical and scapular regions.

iast:
nirīkṣen niścala-dṛśā sūkṣma-lakṣyaṃ samāhitaḥ  /
aśru-sampāta-paryantam ācāryais trāṭakaṃ smṛtam
devanagari:
निरीक्षेन् निश्चल-दृशा सूक्ष्म-लक्ष्यं समाहितः  ।
अश्रु-सम्पात-पर्यन्तम् आचार्यैस् त्राटकं स्मृतम्
english: Being calm, one should gaze steadily at a small mark, till eyes are filled with tears. This is called Trataka by âchâryas.

iast:
mocanaṃ netra-rogāṇāṃ tandādrīṇāṃ kapāṭakam  /
yatnatas trāṭakaṃ gopyaṃ yathā hāṭaka-peṭakam
devanagari:
मोचनं नेत्र-रोगाणां तन्दाद्रीणां कपाटकम्  ।
यत्नतस् त्राटकं गोप्यं यथा हाटक-पेटकम्
english: Trâtaka destroys the eye diseases and removes sloth, etc. It should be kept secret very carefully, like a box of jewellery.

iast:
amandāvarta-vegena tundaṃ savyāpasavyataḥ  /
natāṃso bhrāmayed eṣā nauliḥ siddhaiḥ praśasyate
devanagari:
अमन्दावर्त-वेगेन तुन्दं सव्यापसव्यतः  ।
नतांसो भ्रामयेद् एषा नौलिः सिद्धैः प्रशस्यते
english: Sitting on the toes with heels raised above the ground, and the palms resting on the ground, and in this bent posture the belly is moved forcibly from left to right just, as in vomiting. This is called by adepts the Nauli Karma.

iast:
mandāgni-sandīpana-pācanādi-sandhāpikānanda-karī sadaiva  /
aśeṣa-doṣa-maya-śoṣaṇī ca haṭha-kriyā maulir iyaṃ ca nauliḥ
devanagari:
मन्दाग्नि-सन्दीपन-पाचनादि-सन्धापिकानन्द-करी सदैव  ।
अशेष-दोष-मय-शोषणी च हठ-क्रिया मौलिर् इयं च नौलिः
english: It removes dyspepsia, increases appetite and digestion, and is like the goddess of creation, and causes happiness. It dries up all the disorders. This Nauli is an excellent exercise in Haṭha Yoga.

iast:
bhastrāval loha-kārasya reca-pūrau sasambhramau  /
kapālabhātir vikhyātā kapha-doṣa-viśoṣaṇī
devanagari:
भस्त्रावल् लोह-कारस्य रेच-पूरौ ससम्भ्रमौ  ।
कपालभातिर् विख्याता कफ-दोष-विशोषणी
english: When inhalation and exhalation are performed very quickly, like a pair of bellows of a blacksmith, it dries up all the disorders from the excess of phlegm, and is known as Kapâla Bhâti.

iast:
ṣaṭ-karma-nirgata-sthaulya-kapha-doṣa-malādikaḥ  /
prāṇāyāmaṃ tataḥ kuryād anāyāsena siddhyati
devanagari:
षट्-कर्म-निर्गत-स्थौल्य-कफ-दोष-मलादिकः  ।
प्राणायामं ततः कुर्याद् अनायासेन सिद्ध्यति
english: When Prâṇâyâma is performed after getting rid of obesity born of the defects phlegm, by the performance of the six duties, it easily brings success

iast:
prāṇāyāmair eva sarve praśuṣyanti malā iti  /
ācāryāṇāṃ tu keṣāṃcid anyat karma na saṃmatam
devanagari:
प्राणायामैर् एव सर्वे प्रशुष्यन्ति मला इति  ।
आचार्याणां तु केषांचिद् अन्यत् कर्म न संमतम्
english: Some âchâryâs (teachers) do not advocate any other practice, being of opinion that all the impurities are dried up by the practice of Prâṇâyâma.

iast:
udara-gata-padārtham udvamanti
pavanam apānam udīrya kaṇṭha-nāle  /
krama-paricaya-vaśya-nāḍi-cakrā
gaja-karaṇīti nigadyate haṭhajñaiḥ
devanagari:
उदर-गत-पदार्थम् उद्वमन्ति
पवनम् अपानम् उदीर्य कण्ठ-नाले  ।
क्रम-परिचय-वश्य-नाडि-चक्रा
गज-करणीति निगद्यते हठज्ञैः
english: By carrying the Apâna Vâyû up to the throat, the food, etc., in the stomach are vomited. By degrees, the system of Nâdîs (Śankhinî) becomes known. This is called in Haṭha as Gaja Karaṇi.

iast:
brahmādayo'pi tridaśāḥ pavanābhyāsa-tatparāḥ  /
abhūvann antaka-bhyāt tasmāt pavanam abhyaset
devanagari:
ब्रह्मादयोऽपि त्रिदशाः पवनाभ्यास-तत्पराः  ।
अभूवन्न् अन्तक-भ्यात् तस्मात् पवनम् अभ्यसेत्
english: Brahmâ, and other Devas were always engaged in the exercise of Prâṇâyâma, and, by means of it, got rid of the fear of death. Therefore, one should practise prâṇâyâma regularly.

iast:
yāvad baddho marud dehe yāvac cittaṃ nirākulam  /
yāvad dṛṣṭir bhruvor madhye tāvat kāla-bhayaṃ kutaḥ
devanagari:
यावद् बद्धो मरुद् देहे यावच् चित्तं निराकुलम्  ।
यावद् दृष्टिर् भ्रुवोर् मध्ये तावत् काल-भयं कुतः
english: So long as the breath is restrained in the body, so long as the mind is undisturbed, and so long as the gaze is fixed between the eyebrows, there is no fear from Death.
sourceNotes: Sanskrit Documents has kāla-bhayaṃ śrutaḥ where GRETIL has kāla-bhayaṃ kutaḥ. The latter gives the rhetorical question “whence fear of death?”; the alternative is recorded, not silently substituted.

iast:
vidhivat prāṇa-saṃyāmair nāḍī-cakre viśodhite  /
suṣumṇā-vadanaṃ bhittvā sukhād viśati mārutaḥ
devanagari:
विधिवत् प्राण-संयामैर् नाडी-चक्रे विशोधिते  ।
सुषुम्णा-वदनं भित्त्वा सुखाद् विशति मारुतः
english: When the system of Nâdis becomes clear of the impurities by properly controlling the prâṇa, then the air, piercing the entrance of the Suśumṇâ, enters it easily.

iast:
mārute madhya-saṃcāre manaḥ-sthairyaṃ prajāyate  /
yo manaḥ-susthirī-bhāvaḥ saivāvasthā manonmanī
devanagari:
मारुते मध्य-संचारे मनः-स्थैर्यं प्रजायते  ।
यो मनः-सुस्थिरी-भावः सैवावस्था मनोन्मनी
english: Steadiness of mind comes when the air moves Freely in the middle. That is the manonmanî ( मनोन्मनी ) condition, which is attained when the mind becomes calm.

iast:
tat-siddhaye vidhānajñāś citrān kurvanti kumbhakān  /
vicitra kumbhakābhyāsād vicitrāṃ siddhim āpnuyāt
devanagari:
तत्-सिद्धये विधानज्ञाश् चित्रान् कुर्वन्ति कुम्भकान्  ।
विचित्र कुम्भकाभ्यासाद् विचित्रां सिद्धिम् आप्नुयात्
english: To accomplish it, various Kumbhakas are performed by those who are expert in the methods; for, by the practice of different Kumbhakas, wonderful success is attained.

iast:
sūrya-bhedanam ujjāyī sītkārī śītalī tathā  /
bhastrikā bhrāmarī mūrcchā plāvinīty aṣṭa-kumbhakāḥ
devanagari:
सूर्य-भेदनम् उज्जायी सीत्कारी शीतली तथा  ।
भस्त्रिका भ्रामरी मूर्च्छा प्लाविनीत्य् अष्ट-कुम्भकाः
english: Kumbhakas are of eight kinds, viz., Sûrya Bhedan, Ujjâyî, Sîtkarî, Sîtalî, Bhastrikâ, Bhrâmarî, Mûrchhâ, and Plâvinî.

iast:
pūrakānte tu kartavyo bandho jālandharābhidhaḥ  /
kumbhakānte recakādau kartavyas tūḍḍiyānakaḥ
devanagari:
पूरकान्ते तु कर्तव्यो बन्धो जालन्धराभिधः  ।
कुम्भकान्ते रेचकादौ कर्तव्यस् तूड्डियानकः
english: At the end of Pûraka, Jâlandhara Bandha should be performed, and at the end of Kumbhaka, and at the beginning of Rechaka, Uddiyâna Bandha should be performed.

iast:
adhastāt kuñcanenāśu kaṇṭha-saṅkocane kṛte  /
madhye paścima-tānena syāt prāṇo brahma-nāḍigaḥ
devanagari:
अधस्तात् कुञ्चनेनाशु कण्ठ-सङ्कोचने कृते  ।
मध्ये पश्चिम-तानेन स्यात् प्राणो ब्रह्म-नाडिगः
english: By drawing up from below (Mûla Bandha) and contracting the throat (Jâlandhara Bandha) and by pulling back the middle of the front portion of the body ( i.e. , belly), the Prâṇa goes to the Brahma Nâdî (Suṣumnâ).

iast:
āpānam ūrdhvam utthāpya prāṇaṃ kaṇṭhād adho nayet  /
yogī jarā-vimuktaḥ san ṣoḍaśābda-vayā bhavet
devanagari:
आपानम् ऊर्ध्वम् उत्थाप्य प्राणं कण्ठाद् अधो नयेत्  ।
योगी जरा-विमुक्तः सन् षोडशाब्द-वया भवेत्
english: By pulling up the Apâna Vâyu and by forcing the Prâṇa Vâyu down the throat, the Yogî, liberated from old age, becomes young, as it were 16 years old.

iast:
āsane sukhade yogī baddhvā caivāsanaṃ tataḥ  /
dakṣa-nāḍyā samākṛṣya bahiḥsthaṃ pavanaṃ śanaiḥ
devanagari:
आसने सुखदे योगी बद्ध्वा चैवासनं ततः  ।
दक्ष-नाड्या समाकृष्य बहिःस्थं पवनं शनैः
english: Taking any comfortable posture and performing the âsana, the Yogî should draw in the air slowly, through the right nostril.

iast:
ākeśād ānakhāgrāc ca nirodhāvadhi kumbhayet  /
tataḥ śanaiḥ savya-nāḍyā recayet pavanaṃ śanaiḥ
devanagari:
आकेशाद् आनखाग्राच् च निरोधावधि कुम्भयेत्  ।
ततः शनैः सव्य-नाड्या रेचयेत् पवनं शनैः
english: Then it should be confined within, so that it fills from the nails to the tips of the hair, and then let out through the left nostril slowly.

iast:
kapāla-śodhanaṃ vāta-doṣa-ghnaṃ kṛmi-doṣa-hṛt  /
punaḥ punar idaṃ kāryaṃ sūrya-bhedanam uttamam
devanagari:
कपाल-शोधनं वात-दोष-घ्नं कृमि-दोष-हृत्  ।
पुनः पुनर् इदं कार्यं सूर्य-भेदनम् उत्तमम्
english: This excellent Sûrya Bhedana cleanses the forehead (frontal sinuses), destroys the disorders of Vâta, and removes the worms, and, therefore, it should be performed again and again.

iast:
mukhaṃ saṃyamya nāḍībhyām ākṛṣya pavanaṃ śanaiḥ  /
yathā lagati kaṇṭhāt tu hṛdayāvadhi sa-svanam
devanagari:
मुखं संयम्य नाडीभ्याम् आकृष्य पवनं शनैः  ।
यथा लगति कण्ठात् तु हृदयावधि स-स्वनम्
english: Having closed the opening of the Nâdî (Larynx), the air should be drawn in such a way that it goes touching from the throat to the chest, and making noise while passing.

iast:
pūrvavat kumbhayet prāṇaṃ recayed iḍayā tathā  /
śleṣma-doṣa-haraṃ kaṇṭhe dehānala-vivardhanam
devanagari:
पूर्ववत् कुम्भयेत् प्राणं रेचयेद् इडया तथा  ।
श्लेष्म-दोष-हरं कण्ठे देहानल-विवर्धनम्
english: It should be restrained, as before, and then let out through Idâ (the left nostril). This removes śleṣmâ (phlegm) in the throat and increases the appetite.

iast:
nāḍī-jalodarādhātu-gata-doṣa-vināśanam  /
gacchatā tiṣṭhatā kāryam ujjāyy ākhyaṃ tu kumbhakam
devanagari:
नाडी-जलोदराधातु-गत-दोष-विनाशनम्  ।
गच्छता तिष्ठता कार्यम् उज्जाय्य् आख्यं तु कुम्भकम्
english: It destroys the defects of the nâdîs, dropsy and disorders of Dhâtu (humours). Ujjâyî should be performed in all conditions of life, even while walking or sitting.

iast:
sītkāṃ kuryāt tathā vaktre ghrāṇenaiva vijṛmbhikām  /
evam abhyāsa-yogena kāma-devo dvitīyakaḥ
devanagari:
सीत्कां कुर्यात् तथा वक्त्रे घ्राणेनैव विजृम्भिकाम्  ।
एवम् अभ्यास-योगेन काम-देवो द्वितीयकः
english: Sîtkârî is performed by drawing in the air through the mouth, keeping the tongue between the lips. The air thus drawn in should not be expelled through the mouth. By practising in this way, one becomes next to the God of Love in beauty.
sourceNotes: Corrected the earlier draft’s “draw through the nose”: Sinh explicitly interprets the nasal action as expulsion. The critical edition discusses this as sītkārī at 2.54, with a different first half-verse.

iast:
yoginī cakra-saṃmānyaḥ sṛṣṭi-saṃhāra-kārakaḥ  /
na kṣudhā na tṛṣā nidrā naivālasyaṃ prajāyate
devanagari:
योगिनी चक्र-संमान्यः सृष्टि-संहार-कारकः  ।
न क्षुधा न तृषा निद्रा नैवालस्यं प्रजायते
english: He is regarded adorable by the Yoginîs and becomes the destroyer of the cycle of creation, He is not afflicted with hunger, thirst, sleep or lassitude.

iast:
bhavet sattvaṃ ca dehasya sarvopadrava-varjitaḥ  /
anena vidhinā satyaṃ yogīndro bhūmi-maṇḍale
devanagari:
भवेत् सत्त्वं च देहस्य सर्वोपद्रव-वर्जितः  ।
अनेन विधिना सत्यं योगीन्द्रो भूमि-मण्डले
english: The Satwa of his body becomes free from all the disturbances. In truth, he becomes the lord of the Yogîs in this world.

iast:
jihvayā vāyum ākṛṣya pūrvavat kumbha-sādhanam  /
śanakair ghrāṇa-randhrābhyāṃ recayet pavanaṃ sudhīḥ
devanagari:
जिह्वया वायुम् आकृष्य पूर्ववत् कुम्भ-साधनम्  ।
शनकैर् घ्राण-रन्ध्राभ्यां रेचयेत् पवनं सुधीः
english: As in the above (Sîtkári), the tongue to be protruded a little out of the lips, when the air is drawn in. It is kept confined, as before, and then expelled slowly through the nostrils.

iast:
gulma-plīhādikān rogān jvaraṃ pittaṃ kṣudhāṃ tṛṣām  /
viṣāṇi śītalī nāma kumbhikeyaṃ nihanti hi
devanagari:
गुल्म-प्लीहादिकान् रोगान् ज्वरं पित्तं क्षुधां तृषाम्  ।
विषाणि शीतली नाम कुम्भिकेयं निहन्ति हि
english: This Śîtalî Ḳumbhikâ cures colic, (enlarged) spleen, fever, disorders of bile, hunger, thirst, and counteracts poisons.

iast:
ūrvor upari saṃsthāpya śubhe pāda-tale ubhe  /
padmāsanaṃ bhaved etat sarva-pāpa-praṇāśanam
devanagari:
ऊर्वोर् उपरि संस्थाप्य शुभे पाद-तले उभे  ।
पद्मासनं भवेद् एतत् सर्व-पाप-प्रणाशनम्
english: The Padma Âsana consists in crossing the feet and placing them on both the thighs; it is the destroyer of all sins.

iast:
samyak padmāsanaṃ baddhvā sama-grīvodaraḥ sudhīḥ  /
mukhaṃ saṃyamya yatnena prāṇaṃ ghrāṇena recayet
devanagari:
सम्यक् पद्मासनं बद्ध्वा सम-ग्रीवोदरः सुधीः  ।
मुखं संयम्य यत्नेन प्राणं घ्राणेन रेचयेत्
english: Binding the Padma-Âsana and keeping the body straight, closing the mouth carefully, let the air be expelled through the nose.

iast:
yathā lagati hṛt-kaṇṭhe kapālāvadhi sa-svanam  /
vegena pūrayec cāpi hṛt-padmāvadhi mārutam
devanagari:
यथा लगति हृत्-कण्ठे कपालावधि स-स्वनम्  ।
वेगेन पूरयेच् चापि हृत्-पद्मावधि मारुतम्
english: It should be filled up to the lotus of the heart, by drawing it in with force, making noise and touching the throat, the chest and the head.

iast:
punar virecayet tadvat pūrayec ca punaḥ punaḥ  /
yathaiva lohakāreṇa bhastrā vegena cālyate
devanagari:
पुनर् विरेचयेत् तद्वत् पूरयेच् च पुनः पुनः  ।
यथैव लोहकारेण भस्त्रा वेगेन चाल्यते
english: It should he expelled again and filled again and again as before, just as a pair of bellows of the blacksmith is worked.

iast:
tathaiva sva-śarīra-sthaṃ cālayet pavanaṃ dhiyā  /
yadā śramo bhaved dehe tadā sūryeṇa pūrayet
devanagari:
तथैव स्व-शरीर-स्थं चालयेत् पवनं धिया  ।
यदा श्रमो भवेद् देहे तदा सूर्येण पूरयेत्
english: In the same way, the air of the body should be moved intelligently, filling it through Sûrya when fatigue is experienced.

iast:
yathodaraṃ bhavet pūrṇam anilena tathā laghu  /
dhārayen nāsikāṃ madhyā-tarjanībhyāṃ vinā dṛḍham
devanagari:
यथोदरं भवेत् पूर्णम् अनिलेन तथा लघु  ।
धारयेन् नासिकां मध्या-तर्जनीभ्यां विना दृढम्
english: The air should be drawn in through the right nostril by pressing the thumb against the left side of the nose, so as to close the left nostril; and when filled to the full, it should be closed with the fourth finger (the one next to the little finger) and kept confined.

iast:
vidhivat kumbhakaṃ kṛtvā recayed iḍayānilam  /
vāta-pitta-śleṣma-haraṃ śarīrāgni-vivardhanam
devanagari:
विधिवत् कुम्भकं कृत्वा रेचयेद् इडयानिलम्  ।
वात-पित्त-श्लेष्म-हरं शरीराग्नि-विवर्धनम्
english: Having confined it properly, it should be expelled through the Idâ (left nostril). This destroys Vâta, pitta (bile) and phlegm and increases the digestive power (the gastric fire).

iast:
kuṇḍalī bodhakaṃ kṣipraṃ pavanaṃ sukhadaṃ hitam  /
brahma-nāḍī-mukhe saṃstha-kaphādy-argala-nāśanam
devanagari:
कुण्डली बोधकं क्षिप्रं पवनं सुखदं हितम्  ।
ब्रह्म-नाडी-मुखे संस्थ-कफाद्य्-अर्गल-नाशनम्
english: It quickly awakens the Kuṇḍalinî, purifies the system, gives pleasure, and is beneficial. It destroys phlegm and the impurities accumulated at the entrance of the Brahma Nâdî.

iast:
samyag gātra-samudbhūta-granthi-traya-vibhedakam  /
viśeṣeṇaiva kartavyaṃ bhastrākhyaṃ kumbhakaṃ tv idam
devanagari:
सम्यग् गात्र-समुद्भूत-ग्रन्थि-त्रय-विभेदकम्  ।
विशेषेणैव कर्तव्यं भस्त्राख्यं कुम्भकं त्व् इदम्
english: This Bhastrikâ should be performed plentifully, for it breaks the three knots: Brahma granthi (in the chest), Viṣṇu granthi (in the throat), and Rudra granthi (between the eyebrows) of the body.

iast:
vegād ghoṣaṃ pūrakaṃ bhṛṅga-nādaṃ
bhṛṅgī-nādaṃ recakaṃ manda-mandam  /
yogīndrāṇī̀am evam abhyāsa-yogāc
citte jātā kācid ānanda-līlā
devanagari:
वेगाद् घोषं पूरकं भृङ्ग-नादं
भृङ्गी-नादं रेचकं मन्द-मन्दम्  ।
योगीन्द्राणी̀अम् एवम् अभ्यास-योगाच्
चित्ते जाता काचिद् आनन्द-लीला
english: By filling the air with force, making noise like Bhringi (wasp), and expelling it slowly, making noise in the same way; this practice causes a sort of ecstacy in the minds of Yogîndras.
sourceNotes: Source reads yogīndrāṇī̀am, an anomalous form with a combining grave accent; compare yogīndrāṇām. The source spelling is preserved.
Sanskrit Documents and the critical edition (2.69) support yogīndrāṇām against GRETIL’s corrupt yogīndrāṇī̀am. The draft uses that supported genitive plural; the source display remains diplomatic.

iast:
pūrakānte gāḍhataraṃ baddhvā jālandharaṃ śanaiḥ  /
recayen mūrcchākhyeyaṃ mano-mūrcchā sukha-pradā
devanagari:
पूरकान्ते गाढतरं बद्ध्वा जालन्धरं शनैः  ।
रेचयेन् मूर्च्छाख्येयं मनो-मूर्च्छा सुख-प्रदा
english: Closing the passages with Jâlandhar Bandha firmly at the end of Pûraka, and expelling the air slowly, is called Mûrchhâ, from its causing the mind to swoon and giving comfort.

iast:
antaḥ pravartitodāra-mārutāpūritodaraḥ  /
payasy agādhe'pi sukhāt plavate padma-patravat
devanagari:
अन्तः प्रवर्तितोदार-मारुतापूरितोदरः  ।
पयस्य् अगाधेऽपि सुखात् प्लवते पद्म-पत्रवत्
english: When the belly is filled with air and the inside of the body is filled to its utmost with air, the body floats on the deepest water, like the leaf of a lotus.

iast:
prāṇāyāmas tridhā prokto reca-pūraka-kumbhakaiḥ  /
sahitaḥ kevalaś ceti kumbhako dvividho mataḥ
devanagari:
प्राणायामस् त्रिधा प्रोक्तो रेच-पूरक-कुम्भकैः  ।
सहितः केवलश् चेति कुम्भको द्विविधो मतः
english: Considering Pûraka (Filling), Rechaka (expelling) and Kumbhaka (confining), Prâṇâyâma is of three kinds, but considering it accompanied by Pûraka and Rechaka, and without these, it is of two kinds only, i.e. , Sahita (with) and Kevala (alone).

iast:
yāvat kevala-siddhiḥ syāt sahitaṃ tāvad abhyaset  /
recakaṃ pūrakaṃ muktvā sukhaṃ yad vāyu-dhāraṇam
devanagari:
यावत् केवल-सिद्धिः स्यात् सहितं तावद् अभ्यसेत्  ।
रेचकं पूरकं मुक्त्वा सुखं यद् वायु-धारणम्
english: Exercise in Sahita should be continued till success in Kevala is gained. This latter is simply confining the air with ease, without Rechaka and Pûraka.

iast:
prāṇāyāmo'yam ity uktaḥ sa vai kevala-kumbhakaḥ  /
kumbhake kevale siddhe reca-pūraka-varjite
devanagari:
प्राणायामोऽयम् इत्य् उक्तः स वै केवल-कुम्भकः  ।
कुम्भके केवले सिद्धे रेच-पूरक-वर्जिते
english: In the practice of Kevala Prâṇâyâma when it can be performed successfully without Rechaka and Pûraka, then it is called Kevala Kumbhaka.

iast:
na tasya durlabhaṃ kiṃcit triṣu lokeṣu vidyate  /
śaktaḥ kevala-kumbhena yatheṣṭaṃ vāyu-dhāraṇāt
devanagari:
न तस्य दुर्लभं किंचित् त्रिषु लोकेषु विद्यते  ।
शक्तः केवल-कुम्भेन यथेष्टं वायु-धारणात्
english: There is nothing in the three worlds which may be difficult to obtain for him who is able to keep the air confined according to pleasure, by means of Kevala Kumbhaka.

iast:
rāja-yoga-padaṃ cāpi labhate nātra saṃśayaḥ  /
kumbhakāt kuṇḍalī-bodhaḥ kuṇḍalī-bodhato bhavet  /
anargalā suṣumṇā ca haṭha-siddhiś ca jāyate
devanagari:
राज-योग-पदं चापि लभते नात्र संशयः  ।
कुम्भकात् कुण्डली-बोधः कुण्डली-बोधतो भवेत्  ।
अनर्गला सुषुम्णा च हठ-सिद्धिश् च जायते
english: He obtains the position of Râja Yoga undoubtedly. Kuṇḍalinî awakens by Kumbhaka, and by its awakening, Suṣumnâ becomes free from impurities.

iast:
haṭhaṃ vinā rājayogo rāja-yogaṃ vinā haṭhaḥ  /
na sidhyati tato yugmam āniṣpatteḥ samabhyaset
devanagari:
हठं विना राजयोगो राज-योगं विना हठः  ।
न सिध्यति ततो युग्मम् आनिष्पत्तेः समभ्यसेत्
english: No success in Râja Yoga without Haṭha Yoga, and no success in Haṭha Yoga without Râja Yoga. One should, therefore, practise both of these well, till complete success is gained.

iast:
kumbhaka-prāṇa-rodhānte kuryāc cittaṃ nirāśrayam  /
evam abhyāsa-yogena rāja-yoga-padaṃ vrajet
devanagari:
कुम्भक-प्राण-रोधान्ते कुर्याच् चित्तं निराश्रयम्  ।
एवम् अभ्यास-योगेन राज-योग-पदं व्रजेत्
english: On the completion of Kumbhaka, the mind should be given rest. By practising in this way one is raised to the position of (succeeds in getting) Râja Yoga.

iast:
vapuḥ kṛśatvaṃ vadane prasannatā
nāda-sphuṭatvaṃ nayane sunirmale  /
arogatā bindu-jayo'gni-dīpanaṃ
nāḍī-viśuddhir haṭha-siddhi-lakṣaṇam
devanagari:
वपुः कृशत्वं वदने प्रसन्नता
नाद-स्फुटत्वं नयने सुनिर्मले  ।
अरोगता बिन्दु-जयोऽग्नि-दीपनं
नाडी-विशुद्धिर् हठ-सिद्धि-लक्षणम्
english: When the body becomes lean, the face glows with delight, Anâhatanâda manifests, and eyes are clear, body is healthy, bindu under control, and appetite increases, then one should know that the Nâdîs are purified and success in Haṭha Yoga is approaching.

iast:
sa-śaila-vana-dhātrīṇāṃ yathādhāro'hi-nāyakaḥ  /
sarveṣāṃ yoga-tantrāṇāṃ tathādhāro hi kuṇḍalī
devanagari:
स-शैल-वन-धात्रीणां यथाधारोऽहि-नायकः  ।
सर्वेषां योग-तन्त्राणां तथाधारो हि कुण्डली
english: As the chief of the snakes is the support of the earth with all the mountains and forests on it, so all the Tantras (Yoga practices) rest on the Kuṇḍalinî. (The Vertebral column.)

iast:
suptā guru-prasādena yadā jāgarti kuṇḍalī  /
tadā sarvāṇi padmāni bhidyante granthayo'pi ca
devanagari:
सुप्ता गुरु-प्रसादेन यदा जागर्ति कुण्डली  ।
तदा सर्वाणि पद्मानि भिद्यन्ते ग्रन्थयोऽपि च
english: When the sleeping Kuṇḍalinî awakens by favour of a guru, then all the lotuses (in the six chakras or centres) and all the knots are pierced through.

iast:
prāṇasya śūnya-padavī tadā rājapathāyate  /
tadā cittaṃ nirālambaṃ tadā kālasya vañcanam
devanagari:
प्राणस्य शून्य-पदवी तदा राजपथायते  ।
तदा चित्तं निरालम्बं तदा कालस्य वञ्चनम्
english: Suṣumnâ (Sûnya Padavî) becomes a main road for the passage of Prâṇa, and the mind then becomes free from all connections (with its objects of enjoyments) and Death is then evaded.

iast:
suṣumṇā śūnya-padavī brahma-randhraḥ mahāpathaḥ  /
śmaśānaṃ śāmbhavī madhya-mārgaś cety eka-vācakāḥ
devanagari:
सुषुम्णा शून्य-पदवी ब्रह्म-रन्ध्रः महापथः  ।
श्मशानं शाम्भवी मध्य-मार्गश् चेत्य् एक-वाचकाः
english: Suṣumnâ, Sunya Padavî, Brahma Randhra, Mahâ Patha, Śmaśâna, Śambhavî, Madhya Mârga, are names of one and the same thing.

iast:
tasmāt sarva-prayatnena prabodhayitum īśvarīm  /
brahma-dvāra-mukhe suptāṃ mudrābhyāsaṃ samācaret
devanagari:
तस्मात् सर्व-प्रयत्नेन प्रबोधयितुम् ईश्वरीम्  ।
ब्रह्म-द्वार-मुखे सुप्तां मुद्राभ्यासं समाचरेत्
english: In order, therefore, to awaken this goddess, who is sleeping at the entrance of Brahma Dwâra (the great door), mudrâs should be practised well.

iast:
mahāmudrā mahābandho mahāvedhaś ca khecarī  /
uḍḍīyānaṃ mūlabandhaś ca bandho jālandharābhidhaḥ
devanagari:
महामुद्रा महाबन्धो महावेधश् च खेचरी  ।
उड्डीयानं मूलबन्धश् च बन्धो जालन्धराभिधः
english: Mahâ Mudrâ, Mahâ Bandha, Mahâ Vedha, Khecharî, Uḍḍiyâna Bandha, Mûla Bandha, Jâlandhara Bandha.

iast:
karaṇī viparītākhyā vajrolī śakti-cālanam  /
idaṃ hi mudrā-daśakaṃ jarā-maraṇa-nāśanam
devanagari:
करणी विपरीताख्या वज्रोली शक्ति-चालनम्  ।
इदं हि मुद्रा-दशकं जरा-मरण-नाशनम्
english: Viparîta Karaṇî, Vajroli, and Śakti Châlana. These are the ten Mudrâs which annihilate old age and death.

iast:
ādināthoditaṃ divyam aṣṭaiśvarya-pradāyakam  /
vallabhaṃ sarva-siddhānāṃ durlabhaṃ marutām api
devanagari:
आदिनाथोदितं दिव्यम् अष्टैश्वर्य-प्रदायकम्  ।
वल्लभं सर्व-सिद्धानां दुर्लभं मरुताम् अपि
english: They have been explained by Âdi Nâtha (Śiva) and give eight kinds of divine wealth. They are loved by all the Siddhas and are hard to attain even by the Marutas.

iast:
gopanīyaṃ prayatnena yathā ratna-karaṇḍakam  /
kasyacin naiva vaktavyaṃ kula-strī-surataṃ yathā
devanagari:
गोपनीयं प्रयत्नेन यथा रत्न-करण्डकम्  ।
कस्यचिन् नैव वक्तव्यं कुल-स्त्री-सुरतं यथा
english: These Mudrâs should be kept secret by every means, as one keeps one's box of jewellery, and should, on no account be told to any one, just as husband and wife keep their dealings secret.

iast:
pāda-mūlena vāmena yoniṃ sampīḍya dakṣiṇām  /
prasāritaṃ padaṃ kṛtvā karābhyāṃ dhārayed dṛḍham
devanagari:
पाद-मूलेन वामेन योनिं सम्पीड्य दक्षिणाम्  ।
प्रसारितं पदं कृत्वा कराभ्यां धारयेद् दृढम्
english: Pressing the Yoni (perineum) with the heel of the left foot, and stretching forth the right foot, its toe should be grasped by the thumb and first finger.

iast:
kaṇṭhe bandhaṃ samāropya dhārayed vāyum ūrdhvataḥ  /
yathā daṇḍa-hataḥ sarpo daṇḍākāraḥ prajāyate
devanagari:
कण्ठे बन्धं समारोप्य धारयेद् वायुम् ऊर्ध्वतः  ।
यथा दण्ड-हतः सर्पो दण्डाकारः प्रजायते
english: By stopping the throat (by Jâlandhara Bandha) the air is drawn in from the outside and carried down. Just as a snake struck with a stick becomes straight like a stick, in the same way, śakti (suṣumnâ) becomes straight at once. Then the Kuṇḍalinî, becoming as it were dead, and, leaving both the Idâ and the Pingalâ, enters the suṣumnâ (the middle passage).
translationNote: English and Sanskrit numbering/segmentation differ in the Sinh digitization; the translation is cross-referenced by content. A shared translation may cover more than one verse.
sourceNotes: The historical English’s “carried down” reverses ūrdhvataḥ, “upward”. The snake comparison continues into 3.12; the draft now follows the Sanskrit verse boundary.

iast:
ṛjvībhūtā tathā śaktiḥ kuṇḍalī sahasā bhavet  /
tadā sā maraṇāvasthā jāyate dvipuṭāśrayā
devanagari:
ऋज्वीभूता तथा शक्तिः कुण्डली सहसा भवेत्  ।
तदा सा मरणावस्था जायते द्विपुटाश्रया
english: By stopping the throat (by Jâlandhara Bandha) the air is drawn in from the outside and carried down. Just as a snake struck with a stick becomes straight like a stick, in the same way, śakti (suṣumnâ) becomes straight at once. Then the Kuṇḍalinî, becoming as it were dead, and, leaving both the Idâ and the Pingalâ, enters the suṣumnâ (the middle passage).
translationNote: English and Sanskrit numbering/segmentation differ in the Sinh digitization; the translation is cross-referenced by content. A shared translation may cover more than one verse.
sourceNotes: Rendered separately from 3.11. The identification of the “two passages” with iḍā and piṅgalā is interpretive; the Sanskrit here does not explicitly say “leaves”.

iast:
tataḥ śanaiḥ śanair eva recayen naiva vegataḥ  /
mahā-mudrāṃ ca tenaiva vadanti vibudhottamāḥ
devanagari:
ततः शनैः शनैर् एव रेचयेन् नैव वेगतः  ।
महा-मुद्रां च तेनैव वदन्ति विबुधोत्तमाः
english: It should be expelled then, slowly only and not violently. For this very reason, the best of the wise men call it the Mahâ Mudrâ. This Mahâ Mudrâ has been propounded by great masters.
sourceNotes: Removed a sentence belonging to the beginning of 3.14 that the historical English joins to its preceding verse.

iast:
iyaṃ khalu mahāmudrā mahā-siddhaiḥ pradarśitā  /
mahā-kleśādayo doṣāḥ kṣīyante maraṇādayaḥ  /
mahā-mudrāṃ ca tenaiva vadanti vibudhottamāḥ
devanagari:
इयं खलु महामुद्रा महा-सिद्धैः प्रदर्शिता  ।
महा-क्लेशादयो दोषाः क्षीयन्ते मरणादयः  ।
महा-मुद्रां च तेनैव वदन्ति विबुधोत्तमाः
english: Great evils and pains, like death, are destroyed by it, and for this reason wise men call it the Mahâ Mudrâ.
sourceNotes: Restored the opening clause and preserved the repeated mahāmudrā formula in this GRETIL verse. Other editions segment this passage differently.

iast:
candrāṅge tu samabhyasya sūryāṅge punar abhyaset  /
yāvat-tulyā bhavet saṅkhyā tato mudrāṃ visarjayet
devanagari:
चन्द्राङ्गे तु समभ्यस्य सूर्याङ्गे पुनर् अभ्यसेत्  ।
यावत्-तुल्या भवेत् सङ्ख्या ततो मुद्रां विसर्जयेत्
english: Having practised with the left nostril, it should be practised with the right one; and, when the number on both sides becomes equal, then the mudrâ should be discontinued.
sourceNotes: Replaced the historical English’s nostril-specific wording: candrāṅga and sūryāṅga describe sides or limbs in this posture context; nostrils are not specified.

iast:
na hi pathyam apathyaṃ vā rasāḥ sarve'pi nīrasāḥ  /
api bhuktaṃ viṣaṃ ghoraṃ pīyūṣam api jīryati
devanagari:
न हि पथ्यम् अपथ्यं वा रसाः सर्वेऽपि नीरसाः  ।
अपि भुक्तं विषं घोरं पीयूषम् अपि जीर्यति
english: There is nothing wholesome or injurious; for the practice of this mudrâ destroys the injurious effects of all the rasas (chemicals). Even the deadliest of poisons, if taken, acts like nectar.

iast:
kṣaya-kuṣṭha-gudāvarta-gulmājīrṇa-purogamāḥ  /
tasya doṣāḥ kṣayaṃ yānti mahāmudrāṃ tu yo'bhyaset
devanagari:
क्षय-कुष्ठ-गुदावर्त-गुल्माजीर्ण-पुरोगमाः  ।
तस्य दोषाः क्षयं यान्ति महामुद्रां तु योऽभ्यसेत्
english: Consumption, leprosy, prolapsus anii, colic, and the diseases due to indigestion,—all these irregularities are removed by the practice of this Mahâ Mudrâ.

iast:
kathiteyaṃ mahāmudrā mahā-siddhi-karā nṝṇām  /
gopanīyā prayatnena na deyā yasya kasyacit
devanagari:
कथितेयं महामुद्रा महा-सिद्धि-करा नॄणाम्  ।
गोपनीया प्रयत्नेन न देया यस्य कस्यचित्
english: This Mahâ Mudrâ has been described as the giver of great success (Siddhi) to men. It should be kept secret by every effort, and not revealed to any and everyone.

iast:
pārṣṇiṃ vāmasya pādasya yoni-sthāne niyojayet  /
vāmorūpari saṃsthāpya dakṣiṇaṃ caraṇaṃ tathā
devanagari:
पार्ष्णिं वामस्य पादस्य योनि-स्थाने नियोजयेत्  ।
वामोरूपरि संस्थाप्य दक्षिणं चरणं तथा
english: Press the left heel to the perineum and place the right foot on the left thigh.

iast:
pūrayitvā tato vāyuṃ hṛdaye cubukaṃ dṛḍham  /
niṣpīḍyaṃ vāyum ākuñcya mano-madhye niyojayet
devanagari:
पूरयित्वा ततो वायुं हृदये चुबुकं दृढम्  ।
निष्पीड्यं वायुम् आकुञ्च्य मनो-मध्ये नियोजयेत्
english: Fill in the air, keeping the chin firm against the chest, and, having pressed the air, the mind should he fixed on the middle of the eyebrows or in the suṣumnâ (the spine).

iast:
dhārayitvā yathā-śakti recayed anilaṃ  śanaiḥ  /
savyāṅge tu samabhyasya dakṣāṅge punar abhyaset
devanagari:
धारयित्वा यथा-शक्ति रेचयेद् अनिलं  शनैः  ।
सव्याङ्गे तु समभ्यस्य दक्षाङ्गे पुनर् अभ्यसेत्
english: Having kept it confined so long as possible, it should be expelled slowly. Having practised on the left side, it should be practised on the right side.

iast:
matam atra tu keṣāṃcit kaṇṭha-bandhaṃ vivarjayet  /
rāja-danta-stha-jihvāyā bandhaḥ śasto bhaved iti
devanagari:
मतम् अत्र तु केषांचित् कण्ठ-बन्धं विवर्जयेत्  ।
राज-दन्त-स्थ-जिह्वाया बन्धः शस्तो भवेद् इति
english: Some are of opinion that the closing of throat is not necessary here, for keeping the tongue pressed against the roots of the upper teeth makes a good bandha (stop).

iast:
ayaṃ tu sarva-nāḍīnām ūrdhvaṃ gati-nirodhakaḥ  /
ayaṃ khalu mahā-bandho mahā-siddhi-pradāyakaḥ
devanagari:
अयं तु सर्व-नाडीनाम् ऊर्ध्वं गति-निरोधकः  ।
अयं खलु महा-बन्धो महा-सिद्धि-प्रदायकः
english: This stops the upward motion of all the Nâdîs. Verily this Mahâ Bandha is the giver of great Siddhis.

iast:
kāla-pāśa-mahā-bandha-vimocana-vicakṣaṇaḥ  /
triveṇī-saṅgamaṃ dhatte kedāraṃ prāpayen manaḥ
devanagari:
काल-पाश-महा-बन्ध-विमोचन-विचक्षणः  ।
त्रिवेणी-सङ्गमं धत्ते केदारं प्रापयेन् मनः
english: This Mahâ Bandha is the most skilful means for cutting away the snares of death. It brings about the conjunction of the Trivenî (Idâ, Pingalâ and Suṣumnâ) and carries the mind to Kedâr (the space between the eyebrows, which is the seat of Śiva).

iast:
rūpa-lāvaṇya-sampannā yathā strī puruṣaṃ vinā  /
mahā-mudrā-mahā-bandhau niṣphalau vedha-varjitau
devanagari:
रूप-लावण्य-सम्पन्ना यथा स्त्री पुरुषं विना  ।
महा-मुद्रा-महा-बन्धौ निष्फलौ वेध-वर्जितौ
english: As beauty and loveliness, do not avail a woman without husband, so the Mahâ Mudrâ and the Mahâ-Bandha are useless without the Mahâ Vedha.

iast:
mahā-bandha-sthito yogī kṛtvā pūrakam eka-dhīḥ  /
vāyūnāṃ gatim āvṛtya nibhṛtaṃ kaṇṭha-mudrayā
devanagari:
महा-बन्ध-स्थितो योगी कृत्वा पूरकम् एक-धीः  ।
वायूनां गतिम् आवृत्य निभृतं कण्ठ-मुद्रया
english: Sitting with Mahâ Bandha, the Yogî should fill in the air and keep his mind collected. The movements of the Vâyus (Prâṇa and Apâna) should be stopped by closing the throat.)

iast:
sama-hasta-yugo bhūmau sphicau sanāḍayec chanaiḥ  /
puṭa-dvayam atikramya vāyuḥ sphurati madhyagaḥ
devanagari:
सम-हस्त-युगो भूमौ स्फिचौ सनाडयेच् छनैः  ।
पुट-द्वयम् अतिक्रम्य वायुः स्फुरति मध्यगः
english: Resting both the hands equally on the ground, he should raise himself a little and strike his buttocks against the ground gently. The air, leaving both the passages (Idâ and Pingalâ), starts into the middle one.

iast:
soma-sūryāgni-sambandho jāyate cāmṛtāya vai  /
mṛtāvasthā samutpannā tato vāyuṃ virecayet
devanagari:
सोम-सूर्याग्नि-सम्बन्धो जायते चामृताय वै  ।
मृतावस्था समुत्पन्ना ततो वायुं विरेचयेत्
english: The union of the Idâ and the Pingalâ is effected, in order to bring about immortality. When the air becomes as it were dead (by leaving its course through the Idâ and the Pingalâ) ( i.e. , when it has been kept confined), then it should be expelled.

iast:
mahā-vedho'yam abhyāsān mahā-siddhi-pradāyakaḥ  /
valī-palita-vepa-ghnaḥ sevyate sādhakottamaiḥ
devanagari:
महा-वेधोऽयम् अभ्यासान् महा-सिद्धि-प्रदायकः  ।
वली-पलित-वेप-घ्नः सेव्यते साधकोत्तमैः
english: The practice of this Mahâ Vedha, the giver of great Siddhis, destroys old age, grey hair, and shaking of the body, and therefore it is practised by the best masters.

iast:
etat trayaṃ mahā-guhyaṃ jarā-mṛtyu-vināśanam  /
vahni-vṛddhi-karaṃ caiva hy aṇimādi-guṇa-pradam
devanagari:
एतत् त्रयं महा-गुह्यं जरा-मृत्यु-विनाशनम्  ।
वह्नि-वृद्धि-करं चैव ह्य् अणिमादि-गुण-प्रदम्
english: These THREE are the great secrets. They are the destroyers of old age and death, increase the appetite, confer the accomplishments of Anima, etc.

iast:
aṣṭadhā kriyate caiva yāme yāme dine dine  /
puṇya-saṃbhāra-sandhāya pāpaugha-bhiduraṃ sadā  /
samyak-śikṣāvatām evaṃ svalpaṃ prathama-sādhanam
devanagari:
अष्टधा क्रियते चैव यामे यामे दिने दिने  ।
पुण्य-संभार-सन्धाय पापौघ-भिदुरं सदा  ।
सम्यक्-शिक्षावताम् एवं स्वल्पं प्रथम-साधनम्
english: They should, be practised in 8 ways, daily and hourly. They increase collection of good actions and lessen the evil ones. People, instructed well, should begin their practice, little by little, first.
