sourceNotes: Sanskrit Documents writes prathamasādhanam continuously where GRETIL has prathama-sādhanam; the anusvāra/m difference is a word-final spelling distinction. The critical edition has a differently segmented passage at 3.30–31.

The older English “in 8 ways, daily and hourly” obscures the count and time unit. A yāma is a watch, conventionally about three hours, rather than one hour; the critical edition segments the concluding material differently.

iast:
kapāla-kuhare jihvā praviṣṭā viparītagā  /
bhruvor antargatā dṛṣṭir mudrā bhavati khecarī
devanagari:
कपाल-कुहरे जिह्वा प्रविष्टा विपरीतगा  ।
भ्रुवोर् अन्तर्गता दृष्टिर् मुद्रा भवति खेचरी
english: The Khechari Mudrâ is accomplished by thrusting the tongue into the gullet, by turning it over itself, and keeping the eyesight in the middle of the eyebrows.

iast:
chedana-cālana-dohaiḥ kalāṃ krameṇātha vardhayet tāvat  /
sā yāvad bhrū-madhyaṃ spṛśati tadā khecarī-siddhiḥ
devanagari:
छेदन-चालन-दोहैः कलां क्रमेणाथ वर्धयेत् तावत्  ।
सा यावद् भ्रू-मध्यं स्पृशति तदा खेचरी-सिद्धिः
english: To accomplish this, the tongue is lengthened by cutting the frænum linguæ, moving, and pulling it. When it can touch the space between the eyebrows, then Khechari can be accomplished.

iast:
snuhī-patra-nibhaṃ śastraṃ sutīkṣṇaṃ snigdha-nirmalam  /
samādāya tatas tena roma-mātraṃ samucchinet
devanagari:
स्नुही-पत्र-निभं शस्त्रं सुतीक्ष्णं स्निग्ध-निर्मलम्  ।
समादाय ततस् तेन रोम-मात्रं समुच्छिनेत्
english: Taking a sharp, smooth, and clean instrument, of the shape of a cactus leaf, the frænum of the tongue should be cut a little (as much as a hair's thickness), at a time.

iast:
tataḥ saindhava-pathyābhyāṃ cūrṇitābhyāṃ pragharṣayet  /
punaḥ sapta-dine prāpte roma-mātraṃ samucchinet
devanagari:
ततः सैन्धव-पथ्याभ्यां चूर्णिताभ्यां प्रघर्षयेत्  ।
पुनः सप्त-दिने प्राप्ते रोम-मात्रं समुच्छिनेत्
english: Then rock salt and yellow myrobalan (both powdered) should be rubbed in. On the 7th day, it should again be cut a hair's breadth.

iast:
evaṃ krameṇa ṣaṇ-māsaṃ nityaṃ yuktaḥ samācaret  /
ṣaṇmāsād rasanā-mūla-śirā-bandhaḥ praṇaśyati
devanagari:
एवं क्रमेण षण्-मासं नित्यं युक्तः समाचरेत्  ।
षण्मासाद् रसना-मूल-शिरा-बन्धः प्रणश्यति
english: One should go on doing thus, regularly for six months. At the end of six months, the frænum of the tongue will be completely cut.

iast:
kalāṃ parāṅmukhīṃ kṛtvā tripathe pariyojayet  /
sā bhavet khecarī mudrā vyoma-cakraṃ tad ucyate
devanagari:
कलां पराङ्मुखीं कृत्वा त्रिपथे परियोजयेत्  ।
सा भवेत् खेचरी मुद्रा व्योम-चक्रं तद् उच्यते
english: Turning the tongue upwards, it is fixed on the three ways (œsophagus, windpipe and palate.) Thus it makes the Khechari Mudrâ, and is called the Vyoma Chakra.

iast:
rasanām ūrdhvagāṃ kṛtvā kṣaṇārdham api tiṣṭhati  /
viṣair vimucyate yogī vyādhi-mṛtyu-jarādibhiḥ
devanagari:
रसनाम् ऊर्ध्वगां कृत्वा क्षणार्धम् अपि तिष्ठति  ।
विषैर् विमुच्यते योगी व्याधि-मृत्यु-जरादिभिः
english: The Yogî who sits for a minute turning his tongue upwards, is saved from poisons, diseases, death, old age, etc.

iast:
na rogo maraṇaṃ tandrā na nidrā na kṣudhā tṛṣā  /
na ca mūrcchā bhavet tasya yo mudrāṃ vetti khecarīm
devanagari:
न रोगो मरणं तन्द्रा न निद्रा न क्षुधा तृषा  ।
न च मूर्च्छा भवेत् तस्य यो मुद्रां वेत्ति खेचरीम्
english: He who knows the Khechari Mudrâ is not afflicted with disease, death, sloth, sleep, hunger, thirst, and swooning.

iast:
pīḍyate na sa rogeṇa lipyate na ca karmaṇā  /
bādhyate na sa kālena yo mudrāṃ vetti khecarīm
devanagari:
पीड्यते न स रोगेण लिप्यते न च कर्मणा  ।
बाध्यते न स कालेन यो मुद्रां वेत्ति खेचरीम्
english: He who knows the Khechari Mudrâ, is not troubled by diseases, is not stained with karmas, and is not snared by time.

iast:
cittaṃ carati khe yasmāj jihvā carati khe gatā  /
tenaiṣā khecarī nāma mudrā siddhair nirūpitā
devanagari:
चित्तं चरति खे यस्माज् जिह्वा चरति खे गता  ।
तेनैषा खेचरी नाम मुद्रा सिद्धैर् निरूपिता
english: The Siddhas have devised this Khechari Mudrâ from the fact that the mind and the tongue reach âkâśa by its practice.

iast:
khecaryā mudritaṃ yena vivaraṃ lambikordhvataḥ  /
na tasya kṣarate binduḥ kāminyāḥ śleṣitasya ca
devanagari:
खेचर्या मुद्रितं येन विवरं लम्बिकोर्ध्वतः  ।
न तस्य क्षरते बिन्दुः कामिन्याः श्लेषितस्य च
english: If the hole behind the palate be stopped with Khechari by turning the tongue upwards, then bindu cannot leave its place even if a woman were embraced.

iast:
calito'pi yadā binduḥ samprāpto yoni-maṇḍalam  /
vrajaty ūrdhvaṃ hṛtaḥ śaktyā nibaddho yoni-mudrayā
devanagari:
चलितोऽपि यदा बिन्दुः सम्प्राप्तो योनि-मण्डलम्  ।
व्रजत्य् ऊर्ध्वं हृतः शक्त्या निबद्धो योनि-मुद्रया
english: Even when bindu has moved and reached the region of the yoni, held by yoni-mudrā and drawn by śakti it moves upward.
translationNote: Original literal study rendering; this verse has no corresponding translation in the imported Sinh English text. Technical terms retain their Sanskrit forms. Not independently reviewed.

iast:
ūrdhva-jihvaḥ sthiro bhūtvā somapānaṃ karoti yaḥ  /
māsārdhena na sandeho mṛtyuṃ jayati yogavit
devanagari:
ऊर्ध्व-जिह्वः स्थिरो भूत्वा सोमपानं करोति यः  ।
मासार्धेन न सन्देहो मृत्युं जयति योगवित्
english: If the Yogî drinks Somarasa (juice) by sitting with the tongue turned backwards and mind concentrated, there is no doubt he conquers death within 15 days.
translationNote: English and Sanskrit numbering/segmentation differ in the Sinh digitization; the translation is cross-referenced by content. A shared translation may cover more than one verse.

iast:
nityaṃ soma-kalā-pūrṇaṃ śarīraṃ yasya yoginaḥ  /
takṣakeṇāpi daṣṭasya viṣaṃ tasya na sarpati
devanagari:
नित्यं सोम-कला-पूर्णं शरीरं यस्य योगिनः  ।
तक्षकेणापि दष्टस्य विषं तस्य न सर्पति
english: If the Yogî, whose body is full of Somarasa (juice), were bitten by Takshaka (snake), its poison cannot permeate his body.
translationNote: English and Sanskrit numbering/segmentation differ in the Sinh digitization; the translation is cross-referenced by content. A shared translation may cover more than one verse.

iast:
indhanāni yathā vahnis taila-varti ca dīpakaḥ  /
tathā soma-kalā-pūrṇaṃ dehī dehaṃ na muñcati
devanagari:
इन्धनानि यथा वह्निस् तैल-वर्ति च दीपकः  ।
तथा सोम-कला-पूर्णं देही देहं न मुञ्चति
english: As fire is inseparably connected with the wood and light is connected with the wick and oil, so does the soul not leave the body full of nectar exuding from the Soma.
translationNote: English and Sanskrit numbering/segmentation differ in the Sinh digitization; the translation is cross-referenced by content. A shared translation may cover more than one verse.

iast:
gomāṃsaṃ bhakṣayen nityaṃ pibed amara-vāruṇīm  /
kulīnaṃ tam ahaṃ manye cetare kula-ghātakāḥ
devanagari:
गोमांसं भक्षयेन् नित्यं पिबेद् अमर-वारुणीम्  ।
कुलीनं तम् अहं मन्ये चेतरे कुल-घातकाः
english: Those who eat the flesh of the cow and drink the immortal liquor daily, are regarded by me men of noble family. Others are but a disgrace to their families.
translationNote: English and Sanskrit numbering/segmentation differ in the Sinh digitization; the translation is cross-referenced by content. A shared translation may cover more than one verse.

iast:
go-śabdenoditā jihvā tat praveśo hi tāluni  /
go-māṃsa-bhakṣaṇaṃ tat tu mahā-pātaka-nāśanam
devanagari:
गो-शब्देनोदिता जिह्वा तत् प्रवेशो हि तालुनि  ।
गो-मांस-भक्षणं तत् तु महा-पातक-नाशनम्
english: The word गी means tongue; eating it is thrusting it in the gullet which destroys great sins.
translationNote: English and Sanskrit numbering/segmentation differ in the Sinh digitization; the translation is cross-referenced by content. A shared translation may cover more than one verse.
sourceNotes: The imported English digitization prints गी for the word discussed. The Sanskrit reads go (गो); this appears to be a digitization error in the translation.
Corrected the mirror’s गी to the Sanskrit go and retained tālu as palate; “gullet” is an interpretive expansion in the historical English.

iast:
jihvā-praveśa-sambhūta-vahninotpāditaḥ khalu  /
candrāt sravati yaḥ sāraḥ sā syād amara-vāruṇī
devanagari:
जिह्वा-प्रवेश-सम्भूत-वह्निनोत्पादितः खलु  ।
चन्द्रात् स्रवति यः सारः सा स्याद् अमर-वारुणी
english: Immortal liquor is the nectar exuding from the moon (Chandra situated on the left side of the space between the eyebrows). It is produced by the fire which is generated by thrusting the tongue.
translationNote: English and Sanskrit numbering/segmentation differ in the Sinh digitization; the translation is cross-referenced by content. A shared translation may cover more than one verse.

iast:
cumbantī yadi lambikāgram aniśaṃ jihvā-rasa-syandinī
sa-kṣārā kaṭukāmla-dugdha-sadṛśī madhvājya-tulyā tathā  /
vyādhīnāṃ haraṇaṃ jarānta-karaṇaṃ śastrāgamodīraṇaṃ
tasya syād amaratvam aṣṭa-guṇitaṃ siddhāṅganākarṣaṇam
devanagari:
चुम्बन्ती यदि लम्बिकाग्रम् अनिशं जिह्वा-रस-स्यन्दिनी
स-क्षारा कटुकाम्ल-दुग्ध-सदृशी मध्वाज्य-तुल्या तथा  ।
व्याधीनां हरणं जरान्त-करणं शस्त्रागमोदीरणं
तस्य स्याद् अमरत्वम् अष्ट-गुणितं सिद्धाङ्गनाकर्षणम्

ūrdvhāsyo rasanāṃ niyamya vivare śaktiṃ parāṃ cintayan  /

It should, therefore, be stopped from shedding. This (Khechari Mudrâ) is a very good instrument for this purpose. There is no other means of achieving this end.

सुषुम्णा-वाहिनि प्राणे शून्ये विशति मानसे  ।
तदा सर्वाणि कर्माणि निर्मूलयति योगवित्
english: When the Prâṇa flows in the Suṣumnâ, and the mind has entered śûnya, then the Yogî is free from the effects of Karmas.

iast:
amarāya namas tubhyaṃ so'pi kālas tvayā jitaḥ  /
patitaṃ vadane yasya jagad etac carācaram
devanagari:
अमराय नमस् तुभ्यं सोऽपि कालस् त्वया जितः  ।
पतितं वदने यस्य जगद् एतच् चराचरम्
english: O Immortal one (that is, the yogi who has attained to the condition of Samâdhi), I salute thee! Even death itself, into whose mouth the whole of this movable and immovable world has fallen, has been conquered by thee.

iast:
citte samatvam āpanne vāyau vrajati madhyame  /
tadāmarolī vajrolī sahajolī prajāyate
devanagari:
चित्ते समत्वम् आपन्ने वायौ व्रजति मध्यमे  ।
तदामरोली वज्रोली सहजोली प्रजायते
english: Amarolî, Vajrolî and Sahajolî are accomplished when the mind becomes calm and Prâṇa has entered the middle channel.

iast:
jñānaṃ kuto manasi sambhavatīha tāvat
prāṇo'pi jīvati mano mriyate na yāvat  /
prāṇo mano dvayam idaṃ vilayaṃ nayed yo
mokṣaṃ sa gacchati naro na kathaṃcid anyaḥ
devanagari:
ज्ञानं कुतो मनसि सम्भवतीह तावत्
प्राणोऽपि जीवति मनो म्रियते न यावत्  ।
प्राणो मनो द्वयम् इदं विलयं नयेद् यो
मोक्षं स गच्छति नरो न कथंचिद् अन्यः
english: How can it he possible to get knowledge, so long as the Prâṇa is living and the mind has not died? No one else can get mokṣa, except one who can make one's Prâṇa and mind latent.

iast:
jñātvā suṣumṇāsad-bhedaṃ kṛtvā vāyuṃ ca madhyagam  /
sthitvā sadaiva susthāne brahma-randhre nirodhayet
devanagari:
ज्ञात्वा सुषुम्णासद्-भेदं कृत्वा वायुं च मध्यगम्  ।
स्थित्वा सदैव सुस्थाने ब्रह्म-रन्ध्रे निरोधयेत्
english: Always living in a good locality and having known the secret of the Suṣumnâ, which has a middle course, and making the Vâyu move in it., (the Yogî) should restrain the Vâyu in the Brahma randhra.

iast:
sūrya-candramasau dhattaḥ kālaṃ rātrindivātmakam  /
bhoktrī suṣumnā kālasya guhyam etad udāhṛtam
devanagari:
सूर्य-चन्द्रमसौ धत्तः कालं रात्रिन्दिवात्मकम्  ।
भोक्त्री सुषुम्ना कालस्य गुह्यम् एतद् उदाहृतम्
english: Time, in the form of night and day, is made by the sun and the moon. That, the Suṣumnâ devours this time (death) even, is a great secret.

iast:
dvā-saptati-sahasrāṇi nāḍī-dvārāṇi pañjare  /
suṣumṇā śāmbhavī śaktiḥ śeṣās tv eva nirarthakāḥ
devanagari:
द्वा-सप्तति-सहस्राणि नाडी-द्वाराणि पञ्जरे  ।
सुषुम्णा शाम्भवी शक्तिः शेषास् त्व् एव निरर्थकाः
english: In this body there are 72,000 openings of Nâdis; of these, the Suṣumnâ, which has the Śâmhhavî Sakti in it, is the only important one, the rest are useless.

iast:
vāyuḥ paricito yasmād agninā saha kuṇḍalīm  /
bodhayitvā suṣumṇāyāṃ praviśed anirodhataḥ
devanagari:
वायुः परिचितो यस्माद् अग्निना सह कुण्डलीम्  ।
बोधयित्वा सुषुम्णायां प्रविशेद् अनिरोधतः
english: The Vâyu should be made to enter the Suṣumnâ without restraint by him who has practised the control of breathing and has awakened the Kuṇḍali by the (gastric) fire.

iast:
suṣumṇā-vāhini prāṇe siddhyaty eva manonmanī  /
anyathā tv itarābhyāsāḥ prayāsāyaiva yoginām
devanagari:
सुषुम्णा-वाहिनि प्राणे सिद्ध्यत्य् एव मनोन्मनी  ।
अन्यथा त्व् इतराभ्यासाः प्रयासायैव योगिनाम्
english: The Prâṇa, flowing through the Suṣumnâ, brings about the condition of manonmaṇî; other practices are simply futile for the Yogî.

iast:
pavano badhyate yena manas tenaiva badhyate  /
manaś ca badhyate yena pavanas tena badhyate
devanagari:
पवनो बध्यते येन मनस् तेनैव बध्यते  ।
मनश् च बध्यते येन पवनस् तेन बध्यते
english: By whom the breathing has been controlled, by him the activities of the mind also have been controlled; and, conversely, by whom the activities of the mind have been controlled, by him the breathing also has been controlled.

iast:
hetu-dvayaṃ tu cittasya vāsanā ca samīraṇaḥ  /
tayor vinaṣṭa ekasmin tau dvāv api vinaśyataḥ
devanagari:
हेतु-द्वयं तु चित्तस्य वासना च समीरणः  ।
तयोर् विनष्ट एकस्मिन् तौ द्वाव् अपि विनश्यतः
english: There are two causes of the activities of the mind: (1) Vâsanâ (desires) and (2) the respiration (the Prâṇa). Of these, the destruction of the one is the destruction of both.

iast:
mano yatra vilīyeta pavanas tatra līyate  /
pavano līyate yatra manas tatra vilīyate
devanagari:
मनो यत्र विलीयेत पवनस् तत्र लीयते  ।
पवनो लीयते यत्र मनस् तत्र विलीयते
english: Breathing is lessened when the mind becomes absorbed, and the mind becomes absorbed when the Prâṇa is restrained.

iast:
dugdhāmbuvat saṃmilitāv ubhau tau
tulya-kriyau mānasa-mārutau hi  /
yato marut tatra manaḥ-pravṛttir
yato manas tatra marut-pravṛttiḥ
devanagari:
दुग्धाम्बुवत् संमिलिताव् उभौ तौ
तुल्य-क्रियौ मानस-मारुतौ हि  ।
यतो मरुत् तत्र मनः-प्रवृत्तिर्
यतो मनस् तत्र मरुत्-प्रवृत्तिः
english: Both the mind and the breath are united together, like milk and water; and both of them are equal in their activities. Mind begins its activities where there is the breath, and the Parana begins its activities where there is the mind.

iast:
tatraika-nāśād aparasya nāśa
eka-pravṛtter apara-pravṛttiḥ  /
adhvas tayoś cendriya-varga-vṛttiḥ
pradhvas tayor mokṣa-padasya siddhiḥ
devanagari:
तत्रैक-नाशाद् अपरस्य नाश
एक-प्रवृत्तेर् अपर-प्रवृत्तिः  ।
अध्वस् तयोश् चेन्द्रिय-वर्ग-वृत्तिः
प्रध्वस् तयोर् मोक्ष-पदस्य सिद्धिः
english: By the suspension of the one, therefore, comes the suspension of the other, and by the operations of the one are brought about the operations of the other. When they are present, the Indriyas (the senses) remain engaged in their proper functions, and when they become latent then there is moksa.

iast:
rasasya manasaś caiva cañcalatvaṃ svabhāvataḥ  /
raso baddho mano baddhaṃ kiṃ na siddhyati bhūtale
devanagari:
रसस्य मनसश् चैव चञ्चलत्वं स्वभावतः  ।
रसो बद्धो मनो बद्धं किं न सिद्ध्यति भूतले
english: By nature, Mercury and mind are unsteady: there is nothing in the world which cannot be accomplished when these are made steady.

iast:
mūrcchito harate vyādhīn mṛto jīvayati svayam  /
baddhaḥ khecaratāṃ dhatte raso vāyuś ca pārvati
devanagari:
मूर्च्छितो हरते व्याधीन् मृतो जीवयति स्वयम्  ।
बद्धः खेचरतां धत्ते रसो वायुश् च पार्वति
english: O Pârvati! Mercury and breathing, when made steady, destroy diseases and the dead himself comes to life (by their means). By their (proper) control, moving in the air is attained.

iast:
manaḥ sthairyaṃ sthiro vāyus tato binduḥ sthiro bhavet  /
bindu-sthairyāt sadā sattvaṃ piṇḍa-sthairyaṃ prajāyate
devanagari:
मनः स्थैर्यं स्थिरो वायुस् ततो बिन्दुः स्थिरो भवेत्  ।
बिन्दु-स्थैर्यात् सदा सत्त्वं पिण्ड-स्थैर्यं प्रजायते
english: The breathing is calmed when the mind becomes steady and calm; and hence the preservation of bindu . The preservation of this latter makes the satwa established in the body.

iast:
indriyāṇāṃ mano nātho manonāthas tu mārutaḥ  /
mārutasya layo nāthaḥ sa layo nādam āśritaḥ
devanagari:
इन्द्रियाणां मनो नाथो मनोनाथस् तु मारुतः  ।
मारुतस्य लयो नाथः स लयो नादम् आश्रितः
english: Mind is the master of the senses, and the breath is the master of the mind. The breath in its turn is subordinate to the laya (absorption), and that laya depends on the nâda.

iast:
so'yam evāstu mokṣākhyo māstu vāpi matāntare  /
manaḥ-prāṇa-laye kaścid ānandaḥ sampravartate
devanagari:
सोऽयम् एवास्तु मोक्षाख्यो मास्तु वापि मतान्तरे  ।
मनः-प्राण-लये कश्चिद् आनन्दः सम्प्रवर्तते
english: This very laya is what is called mokṣa, or, being a sectarian, you may not call it mokṣa; but when the mind becomes absorbed, a sort of ecstacy is experienced.

iast:
pranaṣṭa-śvāsa-niśvāsaḥ pradhvasta-viṣaya-grahaḥ  /
niśceṣṭo nirvikāraś ca layo jayati yoginām
devanagari:
प्रनष्ट-श्वास-निश्वासः प्रध्वस्त-विषय-ग्रहः  ।
निश्चेष्टो निर्विकारश् च लयो जयति योगिनाम्
english: By the suspension of respiration and the annihilation of the enjoyments of the senses, when the mind becomes devoid of all the activities and remains changeless, then the Yogî attains to the Laya Stage.

iast:
ucchinna-sarva-saṅkalpo niḥśeṣāśeṣa-ceṣṭitaḥ  /
svāvagamyo layaḥ ko'pi jāyate vāg-agocaraḥ
devanagari:
उच्छिन्न-सर्व-सङ्कल्पो निःशेषाशेष-चेष्टितः  ।
स्वावगम्यो लयः कोऽपि जायते वाग्-अगोचरः
english: When all the thoughts and activities are destroyed, then the Laya Stage is produced, to describe which is beyond the power of speech, being known by self-experience alone.

iast:
yatra dṛṣṭir layas tatra bhūtendriya-sanātanī  /
sā śaktir jīva-bhūtānāṃ dve alakṣye layaṃ gate
devanagari:
यत्र दृष्टिर् लयस् तत्र भूतेन्द्रिय-सनातनी  ।
सा शक्तिर् जीव-भूतानां द्वे अलक्ष्ये लयं गते
translationNote: No corresponding English translation occurs in the imported Sinh text. The Sanskrit of this verse requires textual and syntactic review; an uncertain translation has not been supplied.
sourceNotes: The critical edition has a related but materially different verse at 4.4 (also represented in its alternative fourth chapter). It does not license a word-for-word reconstruction of this difficult GRETIL reading. The provisional draft remains qualified, and no Sinh translation is invented.

iast:
layo laya iti prāhuḥ kīdṛśaṃ laya-lakṣaṇam  /
apunar-vāsanotthānāl layo viṣaya-vismṛtiḥ
devanagari:
लयो लय इति प्राहुः कीदृशं लय-लक्षणम्  ।
अपुनर्-वासनोत्थानाल् लयो विषय-विस्मृतिः
english: Laya is simply then forgetting of the objects of senses when the Vâsanâs (desires) do not rise into existence again.
translationNote: English and Sanskrit numbering/segmentation differ in the Sinh digitization; the translation is cross-referenced by content. A shared translation may cover more than one verse.

iast:
veda-śāstra-purāṇāni sāmānya-gaṇikā iva  /
ekaiva śāmbhavī mudrā guptā kula-vadhūr iva
devanagari:
वेद-शास्त्र-पुराणानि सामान्य-गणिका इव  ।
एकैव शाम्भवी मुद्रा गुप्ता कुल-वधूर् इव
english: The Vedas and the Śâstras are like ordinary public women. Śâmhhavî Mudrâ is the one, which is secluded like a respectable lady.
translationNote: English and Sanskrit numbering/segmentation differ in the Sinh digitization; the translation is cross-referenced by content. A shared translation may cover more than one verse.

iast:
antar lakṣyaṃ bahir dṛṣṭir nimeṣonmeṣa-varjitā  /
eṣā sā śāmbhavī mudrā veda-śāstreṣu gopitā
devanagari:
अन्तर् लक्ष्यं बहिर् दृष्टिर् निमेषोन्मेष-वर्जिता  ।
एषा सा शाम्भवी मुद्रा वेद-शास्त्रेषु गोपिता
english: Aiming at Brahman inwardly, while keeping the sight directed to the external objects, without blinking the eyes, is called the Sâmbhavî Mudrâ, hidden in the Vedas and the Sâstras.
translationNote: English and Sanskrit numbering/segmentation differ in the Sinh digitization; the translation is cross-referenced by content. A shared translation may cover more than one verse.

iast:
antar lakṣya-vilīna-citta-pavano yogī yadā vartate
dṛṣṭyā niścala-tārayā bahir adhaḥ paśyann apaśyann api  /
mudreyaṃ khalu śāmbhavī bhavati sā labdhā prasādād guroḥ
śūnyāśūnya-vilakṣaṇaṃ sphurati tat tattvaṃ padaṃ śāmbhavam
devanagari:
अन्तर् लक्ष्य-विलीन-चित्त-पवनो योगी यदा वर्तते
दृष्ट्या निश्चल-तारया बहिर् अधः पश्यन्न् अपश्यन्न् अपि  ।
मुद्रेयं खलु शाम्भवी भवति सा लब्धा प्रसादाद् गुरोः
शून्याशून्य-विलक्षणं स्फुरति तत् तत्त्वं पदं शाम्भवम्
english: When the Yogî remains inwardly attentive to the Brahman, keeping the mind and the Prâṇa absorbed, and the sight steady, as if seeing everything while in reality seeing nothing outside, below, or above, verily then it is called the Sâmbhavî Mudrâ, which is learnt by the favour of a guru . Whatever, wonderful, Sûnya or Asûnya is perceived, is to be regarded as the manifestation of that great Śambhû (Śiva.)
translationNote: English and Sanskrit numbering/segmentation differ in the Sinh digitization; the translation is cross-referenced by content. A shared translation may cover more than one verse.

iast:
śrī-śāmbhavyāś ca khecaryā avasthā-dhāma-bhedataḥ  /
bhavec citta-layānandaḥ śūnye cit-sukha-rūpiṇi
devanagari:
श्री-शाम्भव्याश् च खेचर्या अवस्था-धाम-भेदतः  ।
भवेच् चित्त-लयानन्दः शून्ये चित्-सुख-रूपिणि
english: The two states, the Sâmbhavî and the Khecharî, are different because of their seats (being the heart and the space between the eyebrows respectively); but both cause happiness, for the mind becomes absorbed in the Chita-sukha-Rupa-âtmana which is void.
translationNote: English and Sanskrit numbering/segmentation differ in the Sinh digitization; the translation is cross-referenced by content. A shared translation may cover more than one verse.

iast:
tāre jyotiṣi saṃyojya kiṃcid unnamayed bhruvau  /
pūrva-yogaṃ mano yuñjann unmanī-kārakaḥ kṣaṇāt
devanagari:
तारे ज्योतिषि संयोज्य किंचिद् उन्नमयेद् भ्रुवौ  ।
पूर्व-योगं मनो युञ्जन्न् उन्मनी-कारकः क्षणात्
english: Fix the gaze on the light (seen on the tip of the nose) and raise the eyebrows a little, with the mind contemplating as before (in the Śambhavî Mudrâ, that is, inwardly thinking of Brahma, but apparently looking outside.) This will create the Unmanî avasthâ at once.
translationNote: English and Sanskrit numbering/segmentation differ in the Sinh digitization; the translation is cross-referenced by content. A shared translation may cover more than one verse.

iast:
kecid āgama-jālena kecin nigama-saṅkulaiḥ  /
kecit tarkeṇa muhyanti naiva jānanti tārakam
devanagari:
केचिद् आगम-जालेन केचिन् निगम-सङ्कुलैः  ।
केचित् तर्केण मुह्यन्ति नैव जानन्ति तारकम्
english: Some are devoted to the Vedas, some to Nigama, while others are enwrapt in Logic, but none knows the value of this mudrâ, which enables one to cross the ocean of existence
translationNote: English and Sanskrit numbering/segmentation differ in the Sinh digitization; the translation is cross-referenced by content. A shared translation may cover more than one verse.

iast:
ardhonmīlita-locanaḥ sthira-manā nāsāgra-dattekṣaṇaś
candrārkāv api līnatām upanayan nispanda-bhāvena yaḥ  /
jyotī-rūpam aśeṣa-bījam akhilaṃ dedīpyamānaṃ paraṃ
tattvaṃ tat-padam eti vastu paramaṃ vācyaṃ kim atrādhikam
devanagari:
अर्धोन्मीलित-लोचनः स्थिर-मना नासाग्र-दत्तेक्षणश्
चन्द्रार्काव् अपि लीनताम् उपनयन् निस्पन्द-भावेन यः  ।
ज्योती-रूपम् अशेष-बीजम् अखिलं देदीप्यमानं परं
तत्त्वं तत्-पदम् एति वस्तु परमं वाच्यं किम् अत्राधिकम्
english: With steady calm mind and half closed eyes, fixed on the tip of the nose, stopping the Idâ and the Pingalâ without blinking, he who can see the light which is the all, the seed, the entire brilliant, great Tatwama, approaches Him, who is the great object. What is the use of more talk?
translationNote: English and Sanskrit numbering/segmentation differ in the Sinh digitization; the translation is cross-referenced by content. A shared translation may cover more than one verse.

iast:
divā na pūjayel liṅgaṃ rātrau caiva na pūjayet  /
sarvadā pūjayel liṅgaṃ divārātri-nirodhataḥ
devanagari:
दिवा न पूजयेल् लिङ्गं रात्रौ चैव न पूजयेत्  ।
सर्वदा पूजयेल् लिङ्गं दिवारात्रि-निरोधतः
english: One should not meditate on the Linga ( i.e. , Âtman) in the day ( i.e. , while Sûrya or Pingalâ is working) or at night (when Idâ is working), but should always contemplate after restraining both.
translationNote: English and Sanskrit numbering/segmentation differ in the Sinh digitization; the translation is cross-referenced by content. A shared translation may cover more than one verse.

iast:
savya-dakṣiṇa-nāḍī-stho madhye carati mārutaḥ  /
tiṣṭhate khecarī mudrā tasmin sthāne na saṃśayaḥ
devanagari:
सव्य-दक्षिण-नाडी-स्थो मध्ये चरति मारुतः  ।
तिष्ठते खेचरी मुद्रा तस्मिन् स्थाने न संशयः
english: When the air has ceased to move in the right and the left nostrils, and has begun to flow in the middle path, then the Khecharî Mudrâ, can be accomplished there. There is no doubt of this.
translationNote: English and Sanskrit numbering/segmentation differ in the Sinh digitization; the translation is cross-referenced by content. A shared translation may cover more than one verse.

iast:
iḍā-piṅgalayor madhye śūnyaṃ caivānilaṃ graset  /
tiṣṭhate khecarī mudrā tatra satyaṃ punaḥ punaḥ
devanagari:
